value.zh: 八月，吳遂圍江夏，寇襄陽，大將軍宣帝救襄陽，斬吳將張霸等，兵喪更王之應也。
value.en: In the eighth month Wu besieged Jiangxia and struck Xiangyang; General-in-Chief Xuandi (Sima Yi) rescued Xiangyang and slew Wu generals such as Zhang Ba, matching the omens of war, mourning, and shifting sovereignty.
value.literal: In the eighth month Wu then besieged Jiangxia, raided Xiangyang, and Grand Marshal Xuandi relieved Xiangyang, beheading Wu generals including Zhang Ba—the response of military losses and change of ruler.

value.zh: 少帝正始元年十月乙酉，彗星見西方，在尾，長三丈，拂牽牛，犯太白。
value.en: Wei Zhengshi comet in Tail.
value.literal: On yiyou in the tenth month of Zhengshi 1 of Shaodi a comet appeared in the west at Tail three zhang long, brushing the Herdsman and transgressing the Great White.

value.zh: 十一月甲子，進犯羽林。
value.en: November comet entered Forbidden Guards.
value.literal: On jiazi in the eleventh month it advanced to strike the Forbidden Guards.

value.zh: 占曰：「尾為燕，又為吳，牛亦吳越之分。
value.en: The prognostication said, "Tail is Yan and also Wu, and Ox is also the allotment of Wu-Yue.
value.literal: The omen-text says: “Tail is Yan and also Wu; Ox likewise marks Wu-Yue.

value.zh: 太白為上將，羽林中軍兵。
value.en: Venus is the supreme general, and the Feathered Forest is the central army.
value.literal: The Great White is the upper general; Forbidden Guards are central troops.

value.zh: 為吳越有喪，中軍兵動。」
value.en: It means Wu-Yue will have mourning, and the central army will move."
value.literal: Wu-Yue will mourn while central armies stir.

value.zh: 二年五月，吳遣三將寇邊。
value.en: Year two May Wu raided borders.
value.literal: In the fifth month of the second year Wu dispatched three generals to raid the frontier.

value.zh: 吳太子登卒。
value.en: Wu heir Deng died.
value.literal: Crown Prince Deng of Wu died.

value.zh: 六月，宣帝討諸葛恪於皖。
value.en: June Sima Yi attacked Zhuge Ke.
value.literal: In the sixth month Xuandi campaigned against Zhuge Ke at Wan.

value.zh: 太尉滿寵薨。
value.en: Man Chong, Grand Commandant, passed away.
value.literal: Grand Commandant Man Chong died.

value.zh: 六年八月戊午，彗星見七星，長二尺，色白，進至張，積二十三日滅。
value.en: Zhengshi 6 eighth month: comet in the Seven Stars.
value.literal: On wuwu in the sixth year’s eighth month a comet appeared in the Seven Stars two feet long, white, advancing to Zhang, vanishing after twenty-three days.

value.zh: 七年十一月癸亥，又見軫，長一尺，積百五十六日滅。
value.en: Seventh year November comet in Chariot.
value.literal: On guihai in the eleventh month of the seventh year it again appeared in the Chariot one foot long, lasting 156 days.

value.zh: 九年三月，又見昴，長六尺，色青白，芒西南指。
value.en: Ninth year third month comet in Mao.
value.literal: In the third month of the ninth year it again appeared in the Hairy Head six feet long, bluish white, tail pointing southwest.

value.zh: 七月，又見翼，長二尺，進至軫，積四十二日滅。
value.en: July comet Wings to Chariot.
value.literal: In the seventh month it again appeared in Wings two feet long, reaching the Chariot, disappearing after forty-two days.

value.zh: 案占曰：「七星張為周分野，翼軫為楚，昴為趙魏。
value.en: Examining the prognostication, it said, "Seven Stars and Extended Net are the allotment of Zhou; Wings and Chariot are Chu; Mao is Zhao and Wei.
value.literal: Investigating the gloss: “Seven Stars and Zhang are Zhou’s field; Wings and Chariot are Chu; Mao is Zhao and Wei.

value.zh: 彗所以除舊布新，主兵喪也。」
value.en: Comets are how the old is removed and the new spread; they govern war and mourning."
value.literal: Comets purge old and spread new; they preside over armies and mourning.

value.zh: 嘉平元年，宣帝誅曹爽兄弟及其党與，皆夷三族，京師嚴兵。
value.en: Jiaping 1 Sima Yi purged Cao Shuang.
value.literal: In Jiaping 1 Xuandi executed Cao Shuang’s brothers and faction to the third kin, tightening arms at the capital.

value.zh: 三年，誅楚王彪，又襲王淩於淮南。
value.en: Year three killed Cao Biao and crushed Wang Ling.
value.literal: In the third year he executed Prince Chu Biao and struck Wang Ling in Huainan.

value.zh: 淮南，東楚也。
value.en: Huainan matches Chu.
value.literal: Huainan is eastern Chu.

value.zh: 魏諸王幽於鄴。
value.en: Wei imperial kin were caged at Ye.
value.literal: Wei princes were confined at Ye.

value.zh: 魏明帝景初二年，宣帝圍公孫文懿于襄平。
value.en: In the second year of Jingchu under Emperor Ming of Wei, Sima Yi besieged Gongsun Yuan at Xiangping.
value.literal: In the second year of Jingchu under Emperor Ming of Wei, Emperor Xuan besieged Gongsun Yuan at Xiangping.

value.zh: 八月丙寅夜，有大流星長數十丈，白色有芒鬣，從首山東北流，墜襄平城東南。
value.en: On the night of bingyin in the eighth month, a great meteor tens of zhang long, white with a bristled tail, streamed northeast from Mount Shou and fell southeast of the city of Xiangping.
value.literal: On bingyin night in the eighth month a great meteor tens of zhang long, white with a maned tail, flowed northeast from Mount Shou and fell southeast of Xiangping city.

value.zh: 占曰：「圍城而有流星來走城上及墜城中者破。」
value.en: The prognostication said, "When a city is besieged and a meteor comes and runs above the city or falls within the city, it is broken."
value.literal: The omen-text says: “When besieging a city, meteors flying onto the walls or inside mean the city breaks.

value.zh: 又曰：「星墜，當其下有戰場。」
value.en: It also said, "When a star falls, beneath it there will be a battlefield."
value.literal: It also says: “Where stars fall becomes a battlefield.

value.zh: 又曰：「凡星所墜，國易姓。」
value.en: It also said, "Wherever a star falls, the state changes surnames."
value.literal: It also says: “Whatever land stars fall upon changes surname.

value.zh: 九月，文懿突圍走，至星墜所被斬，屠城，坑其眾。
value.en: In the ninth month Wenyi broke out of the siege, fled to where the star had fallen, and was beheaded; the city was slaughtered and his multitude buried alive.
value.literal: In September Yuan broke out, fled to the fall site, was beheaded, the city slaughtered and buried alive.

value.zh: 五禮之別，二曰凶。
value.en: Among the five canonical rituals, the second category is mourning for the dead.
value.literal: Of the five kinds of ritual, the second is called 'inauspicious' (mourning).

value.zh: 自天子至於庶人，身體髮膚，受之父母，其理既均，其情亦等，生則養，死則哀，故曰三年之喪，天下之達禮者也。
value.en: From the sovereign to the humblest subject, flesh and hair come from one's parents; the duty is the same and the grief no different—while they live we sustain them, when they die we mourn them. Hence the canon calls three years' mourning the rite that runs through all the world.
value.literal: From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, body, skin, and hair are received from father and mother; the principle is uniform and the feeling equal—in life they nurture, in death they mourn; therefore it is said that three years' mourning is the penetrating rite of the realm.

value.zh: 漢禮，天子崩，自不豫至於登遐及葬，喪紀之制，與夫三代變易。
value.en: Han court precedent for an emperor's death—from the first illness through the lying-in-state to interment—shifted its mourning code across the Xia, Shang, and Zhou models.
value.literal: Under Han ritual, when the Son of Heaven collapsed, from the first illness through the final journey to burial, the mourning regulations changed with the Three Dynasties.

value.zh: 魏晉以來，大體同漢。
value.en: From the Wei through the Jin, the dynasty largely kept Han practice.
value.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, the broad pattern matched Han.

value.zh: 然自漢文革喪禮之制，後代遵之，無復三年之禮。
value.en: Yet once Emperor Wen of Han pared the mourning statutes, every succeeding age copied his shortcut, and the full three-year observance disappeared.
value.literal: Yet from Emperor Wen of Han's reform of mourning regulations, later ages followed it and no longer practiced three years' mourning.

value.zh: 及魏武臨終，遺令「天下尚未安定，未得遵古。
value.en: When Wei Wu was near death, he left a command: 'All under Heaven is not yet settled; I cannot follow antiquity.
value.literal: When Wei Wu was near death, he left a command: 'All under Heaven is not yet settled; I cannot follow antiquity.

value.zh: 百官當臨中者，十五舉音，葬畢便除。
value.en: For the hundred officials who should attend at the central halt, raise the dirge fifteen times; when burial is finished, remove mourning at once.
value.literal: For the hundred officials who should attend at the central halt, raise the dirge fifteen times; when burial is finished, remove mourning at once.

value.zh: 其將兵屯戍者，不得離部。」
value.en: Those who command troops on garrison may not leave their commands.'
value.literal: Those who command troops on garrison may not leave their commands.'

value.zh: 魏武以正月庚子崩，辛丑即殯，是月丁卯葬，是為不逾月也。
value.en: Cao Cao died on the gengzi day of the first month; by xinchou the bier stood ready; dingmao that same month saw the interment—mourning lifted inside a single month.
value.literal: Wei Wu died on gengzi in the first month; on xinchou he was encoffined; on dingmao that same month he was buried—this is what is meant by 'not exceeding one month.'

value.zh: 及宣帝、景帝之崩，並從權制。
value.en: The deaths of Sima Yi and Sima Shi were handled under the same shortened schedule.
value.literal: When Emperor Xuan and Emperor Jing died, each likewise followed the expedient code.

value.zh: 文帝之崩，國內服三日。
value.en: When Sima Zhao died, the whole state wore mourning for three days and no more.
value.literal: When Emperor Wen died, the realm observed mourning for three days only.

value.zh: 武帝亦遵漢魏之典，既葬除喪，然猶深衣素冠，降席撤膳。
value.en: Emperor Sima Yan kept the Han–Wei rule of ending court mourning at burial, but he still dressed in plain hemp deep robes, set aside brocade cushions, and ate only coarse fare.
value.literal: Emperor Wu likewise followed Han and Wei precedent: once the burial ended he set aside formal mourning, yet still wore plain deep garments and an undyed cap, lowered his mat, and withdrew rich food from his table.

value.zh: 太宰司馬孚、太傅鄭沖、太保王祥、太尉何曾、司徒領中領軍司馬望、司空荀顗、車騎將軍賈充、尚書令裴秀、尚書僕射武陔、都護大將軍郭建、侍中郭綏、中書監荀勖、中軍將軍羊祜等奏曰：「臣聞禮典軌度，豐殺隨時，虞夏商周，咸不相襲，蓋有由也。
value.en: Grand Preceptor Sima Fu, Grand Tutor Zheng Chong, Grand Guardian Wang Xiang, Grand Commandant He Ceng, Minister of Education concurrently Central Army commander Sima Wang, Minister of Works Xun Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong, Prefect of the Masters of Writing Pei Xiu, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Wu Yan, Chief Protector and Grand General Guo Jian, Palace Attendant Guo Sui, Director of the Palace Secretariat Xun Xu, Central Army General Yang Hu, and others memorialized: 'We have heard that ritual canons and measures wax or wane with the times; the houses of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou never blindly copied one another—each had its reasons.
value.literal: Grand Preceptor Sima Fu, Grand Tutor Zheng Chong, Grand Guardian Wang Xiang, Grand Commandant He Ceng, Minister of Education concurrently Central Army commander Sima Wang, Minister of Works Xun Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong, Prefect of the Masters of Writing Pei Xiu, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Wu Yan, Chief Protector and Grand General Guo Jian, Palace Attendant Guo Sui, Director of the Palace Secretariat Xun Xu, Central Army General Yang Hu, and others memorialized: 'We have heard that ritual canons and measures wax or wane with the times; the houses of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou never blindly copied one another—each had its reasons.

value.zh: 大晉紹承漢魏，有革有因，期於足以興化而已，故未得皆返太素，同規上古也。
value.en: Great Jin inherits Han and Wei with some reforms and some continuities, aiming only to lift custom where it must; therefore it cannot yet return wholesale to pristine antiquity or match high antiquity in a single stroke.
value.literal: Great Jin inherits Han and Wei with some reforms and some continuities, aiming only to lift custom where it must; therefore it cannot yet return wholesale to pristine antiquity or match high antiquity in a single stroke.

value.zh: 陛下既以俯遵漢魏降喪之典，以濟時務，而躬蹈大孝，情過乎哀，素冠深衣，降席撤膳，雖武丁行之于殷世，曾閔履之於布衣，未足以逾。
value.en: Your Majesty has already bowed to Han and Wei's lowered mourning canons to meet pressing affairs, yet you personally tread the utmost filial path; your feeling overshoots moderation—plain cap, deep garments, lowered mat, curtailed meals—even King Wuding in the Yin age or Zengzi and Min Ziqian as commoners did not surpass this.
value.literal: Your Majesty has already bowed to Han and Wei's lowered mourning canons to meet pressing affairs, yet you personally tread the utmost filial path; your feeling overshoots moderation—plain cap, deep garments, lowered mat, curtailed meals—even King Wuding in the Yin age or Zengzi and Min Ziqian as commoners did not surpass this.

value.zh: 方今荊蠻未夷，庶政未乂，萬機事殷，動勞神慮，豈遑全遂聖旨，以從至情。
value.en: Now the southern tribes are not yet pacified, government is not yet ordered, and myriad threads of business press upon you, taxing mind and spirit—how could you wholly indulge sage intent and the utmost of private feeling?
value.literal: Now the southern tribes are not yet pacified, government is not yet ordered, and myriad threads of business press upon you, taxing mind and spirit—how could you wholly indulge sage intent and the utmost of private feeling?

value.zh: 臣等以為陛下宜割情以康時濟俗，輒敕御府易服，內省改坐，太官復膳，諸所施行，皆如舊制。」
value.en: We your servants therefore believe Your Majesty should cut private feeling to heal the age and aid custom; we dare order the Palace Treasury to exchange garments, the inner apartments to restore seating, the Grand Provisioner to restore full meals, and every other measure to follow the standing regulations.'
value.literal: We your servants therefore believe Your Majesty should cut private feeling to heal the age and aid custom; we dare order the Palace Treasury to exchange garments, the inner apartments to restore seating, the Grand Provisioner to restore full meals, and every other measure to follow the standing regulations.'

value.zh: 詔曰：「每感念幽冥，而不得終苴絰於草土，以存此痛，況當食稻衣錦，誠詭然激切其心，非所以相解也。
value.en: The edict replied: 'Whenever I brood on the shades below and realize I cannot finish wearing straw cord on the burial mound to keep this pain alive—how much more to eat polished rice and wear brocade—indeed it stabs the heart; that is no way to console myself.
value.literal: The edict replied: 'Whenever I brood on the shades below and realize I cannot finish wearing straw cord on the burial mound to keep this pain alive—how much more to eat polished rice and wear brocade—indeed it stabs the heart; that is no way to console myself.

value.zh: 吾本諸生家，傳禮來久，何心一旦便易此情於所天！
value.en: I was born to a house of scholars; the rites have been handed down among us a long time—how could my heart one morning cast off this feeling toward him who is my heaven!
value.literal: I was born to a house of scholars; the rites have been handed down among us a long time—how could my heart one morning cast off this feeling toward him who is my heaven!

value.zh: 相從已多，可試省孔子答宰我之言，無事紛紜也。
value.en: You have followed me long; try reviewing Confucius's answer to Zai Wo—do not fuss at me again and again.
value.literal: You have followed me long; try reviewing Confucius's answer to Zai Wo—do not fuss at me again and again.

value.zh: 言及悲剝，柰何！
value.en: When words touch grief it tears the heart—what can be done!
value.literal: When words touch grief it tears the heart—what can be done!

value.zh: 柰何！」
value.en: What can be done!'
value.literal: What can be done!'

value.zh: 孚等重奏：「伏讀聖詔，感以悲懷，輒思仲尼所以抑宰我之問，聖思所以不能已已，甚深甚篤。
value.en: Fu and the others rememorialized: 'We have read the sage edict and are moved to grief; we reflect on why Confucius checked Zai Wo's question—the sage mind cannot stop itself; the feeling is very deep and very earnest.
value.literal: Fu and the others rememorialized: 'We have read the sage edict and are moved to grief; we reflect on why Confucius checked Zai Wo's question—the sage mind cannot stop itself; the feeling is very deep and very earnest.

value.zh: 然今者干戈未戢，武事未偃，萬機至重，天下至眾。
value.en: Yet now weapons are not yet stilled, military affairs not yet rested, the myriad threads are weightiest, and all under Heaven is most numerous.
value.literal: Yet now weapons are not yet stilled, military affairs not yet rested, the myriad threads are weightiest, and all under Heaven is most numerous.

value.zh: 陛下以萬乘之尊，履布衣之禮，服粗席稿，水飲疏食，殷憂內盈，毀悴外表。
value.en: Your Majesty in the honor of ten thousand chariots treads the rites of a commoner—coarse mat and straw padding, drinking water and eating coarse food, sorrow swelling within, emaciation showing without.
value.literal: Your Majesty in the honor of ten thousand chariots treads the rites of a commoner—coarse mat and straw padding, drinking water and eating coarse food, sorrow swelling within, emaciation showing without.

value.zh: 而躬勤萬機，坐而待旦，降心接下，仄不遑食，所以勞力者如斯之甚。
value.en: Yet you personally toil at myriad threads of state, sit awaiting dawn, humble your heart to receive subordinates, and lean so far you have no leisure to eat—such labor of strength is extreme.
value.literal: Yet you personally toil at myriad threads of state, sit awaiting dawn, humble your heart to receive subordinates, and lean so far you have no leisure to eat—such labor of strength is extreme.

value.zh: 是以臣等悚息不寧，誠懼神氣用損，以疚大事。
value.en: Therefore we your servants tremble and breathe uneasily, truly fearing that spirit will be depleted and the great affair harmed.
value.literal: Therefore we your servants tremble and breathe uneasily, truly fearing that spirit will be depleted and the great affair harmed.

value.zh: 輒敕有司，改坐復常，率由舊典。
value.en: We dare order the relevant offices to restore your seat and routine, following the old canons.
value.literal: We dare order the relevant offices to restore your seat and routine, following the old canons.

value.zh: 惟陛下察納愚款，以慰皇太后之心。」
value.en: Only let Your Majesty examine and accept our foolish sincerity, so as to console the heart of the Empress Dowager.'
value.literal: Only let Your Majesty examine and accept our foolish sincerity, so as to console the heart of the Empress Dowager.'

value.zh: 又詔曰：「重覽奏議，益以悲剝，不能自勝，柰何！
value.en: Another edict said: 'Rereading your memorials only deepens the tearing grief; I cannot master myself—what can be done!
value.literal: Another edict said: 'Rereading your memorials only deepens the tearing grief; I cannot master myself—what can be done!

value.zh: 柰何！
value.en: What can be done!
value.literal: What can be done!

value.zh: 三年之喪，自古達禮，誠聖人稱情立衷，明恕而行也。
value.en: Three years' mourning has from antiquity been the penetrating rite of the realm; truly the sages weighed human feeling, set the inner mean, and acted with enlightened forbearance.
value.literal: Three years' mourning has from antiquity been the penetrating rite of the realm; truly the sages weighed human feeling, set the inner mean, and acted with enlightened forbearance.

value.zh: 神靈日遠，無所訴告，雖薄於情，食旨服美，所不堪也。
value.en: The spirits grow daily more distant; there is nowhere to cry complaint—though the outward show be slight, to taste rich food and wear fine cloth is unbearable.
value.literal: The spirits grow daily more distant; there is nowhere to cry complaint—though the outward show be slight, to taste rich food and wear fine cloth is unbearable.

value.zh: 不宜反覆，重傷其心，言用斷絕，柰何！
value.en: You ought not go back and forth and doubly wound this heart; I break off words—what can be done!
value.literal: You ought not go back and forth and doubly wound this heart; I break off words—what can be done!

value.zh: 柰何！」
value.en: What can be done!'
value.literal: What can be done!'

value.zh: 帝遂以此禮終三年。
value.en: With that he carried the full three-year vigil despite every plea.
value.literal: The emperor therefore observed mourning to the full three years under this rite.

value.zh: 後居太后之喪亦如之。
value.en: He repeated the same austerity when the empress dowager died.
value.literal: Later, when mourning the Empress Dowager, he did the same.

value.zh: 宣帝豫自于首陽山為土藏，不填不樹，作《顧命終制》，斂以時服，不設明器。
value.en: Sima Yi dug a plain shaft on Shouyang, left the hill unmarked, and left written orders for everyday clothes and no grave goods.
value.literal: Emperor Xuan in advance prepared an earthen burial chamber on Mount Shouyang—no mound, no trees—and composed the 'Charge at Gu' end testament: shroud in seasonal clothes only, with no ming vessels.

value.zh: 景、文皆謹奉成命，無所加焉。
value.en: Sima Shi and Sima Zhao kept Cao Pi's austere burial instructions to the letter.
value.literal: Emperor Jing and Emperor Wen both scrupulously obeyed the completed testament and added nothing to it.

value.zh: 景帝崩，喪事制度又依宣帝故事。
value.en: Sima Shi's obsequies copied Sima Yi's lean model.
value.literal: When Emperor Jing died, the funeral regulations again followed Emperor Xuan's precedent.

value.zh: 武帝泰始四年，文明王皇后崩，將合葬，開崇陽陵，使太尉司馬望奉祭，進皇帝密璽綬于便房神坐。
value.en: In the fourth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu, when Empress Wenming Wang died and was about to be jointly buried, Chongyang Mausoleum was opened, Grand Commandant Sima Wang was sent to present sacrifice, and the emperor's sealed jade seal and cords were advanced to the spirit seat in the side chamber.
value.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu, when Empress Wenming Wang died and was about to be jointly buried, Chongyang Mausoleum was opened, Grand Commandant Sima Wang was sent to present sacrifice, and the emperor's sealed jade seal and cords were advanced to the spirit seat in the side chamber.

value.zh: 魏氏金璽，此又儉矣。
value.en: Even the golden seal bespoke restraint.
value.literal: Wei's gold seal—another mark of frugality.

value.zh: 江左初，元、明崇儉，且百度草創，山陵奉終，省約備矣。
value.en: When the court fled across the Yangzi, Sima Rui and Sima Shao kept burials modest while institutions were new.
value.literal: Early in the southward court, Emperors Yuan and Ming prized simplicity; the hundred offices were still being founded, so imperial tombs stayed spare yet adequate.

value.zh: 成帝咸康七年，皇后杜氏崩。
value.en: Empress Du of Cheng passed in 341.
value.literal: In the seventh Xiankang year of Emperor Cheng, Empress Du died.

value.zh: 詔外官五日一入臨，內官旦一入而已，過葬虞祭禮畢止。
value.en: Courtiers could wail only on that thin schedule until the post-burial service closed mourning.
value.literal: An edict ordered outer officials to enter condolence only once every five days and inner staff once at dawn, ending once burial and the Yu rite were finished.

value.zh: 有司奏，大行皇后陵所作凶門柏歷門，號顯陽端門。
value.en: The ministry wanted a formal death-gate and cypress lintel named like a palace portal.
value.literal: The offices proposed building a funeral gate and cypress "calendar" portal for the late empress's mound, to be named the Xianyang gate.

value.zh: 詔曰：「門如所處。
value.en: The edict read: "Let the gate stand where proposed.
value.literal: The edict read: "Let the gate stand where proposed.

value.zh: 凶門柏歷，大為煩費，停之。」
value.en: Funeral gates and cypress calendars are extravagantly costly—suspend them."
value.literal: Funeral gates and cypress calendars are extravagantly costly—suspend them."

value.zh: 案蔡謨說，以二瓦器盛始死之祭，繫於木，裹以葦席，置庭中，近南，名為重，今之凶門是其象也。
value.en: Cai Mo traced the "death gate" to the temporary chong bundle hung south of the yard.
value.literal: Cai Mo explains that two earthen jars holding the first-death offerings were lashed to a frame, wrapped in reed matting, and set in the courtyard toward the south as a chong; today's funeral gate imitates that form.

value.zh: 禮，既虞而作主，今未葬，未有主，故以重當之。
value.en: Until the tablet existed, the chong served as the spirit's lodging.
value.literal: By ritual one fashions the spirit tablet after the Yu rite; before burial there is no tablet, so the chong stands in for it.

value.zh: 禮稱為主道，此其義也。
value.en: Classical glosses treat the chong as the spirit's interim path.
value.literal: The canon calls this the "lord-of-the-spirit path"—that is the idea.

value.zh: 范堅又曰：「凶門非禮，禮有懸重，形似凶門。
value.en: Fan Jian adds: "The funeral gate is not canonical; ritual only suspends a chong that merely resembles a gate.
value.literal: Fan Jian adds: "The funeral gate is not canonical; ritual only suspends a chong that merely resembles a gate.

value.zh: 後人出之門外以表喪，俗遂行之。
value.en: Later generations moved it outside the gate to advertise mourning, and vulgar custom adopted it.
value.literal: Later generations moved it outside the gate to advertise mourning, and vulgar custom adopted it.

value.zh: 薄帳，即古弔幕之類也。」
value.en: Thin curtains belong to the ancient class of mourning screens."
value.literal: Thin curtains belong to the ancient class of mourning screens."

value.zh: 是時，又詔曰：「重壤之下，豈宜崇飾無用，陵中唯潔掃而已。」
value.en: Another edict then declared: "Beneath double layers of earth one should not lavish useless ornament; only sweep the vault clean."
value.literal: Another edict then declared: "Beneath double layers of earth one should not lavish useless ornament; only sweep the vault clean."

value.zh: 有司又奏，依舊選公卿以下六品子弟六十人為挽郎，詔又停之。
value.en: Officials wanted sixty noble sons as rope-pullers; the throne again said no.
value.literal: The offices again asked to conscript sixty youths of sixth rank and below as catafalque pullers, as of old; the edict again refused.

value.zh: 孝武帝太元四年九月，皇后王氏崩。
value.en: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu, Empress Wang died.
value.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu, Empress Wang died.

value.zh: 詔曰：「終事唯從儉速。」
value.en: An edict said: "Finish everything frugally and quickly."
value.literal: An edict said: "Finish everything frugally and quickly."

value.zh: 又詔：「遠近不得遣山陵使。」
value.en: Another edict said, “Neither near nor distant officials may send envoys to the imperial tombs.”
value.literal: Another edict said, “Neither near nor distant officials may send envoys to the imperial tombs.”

value.zh: 有司奏選挽郎二十四人，詔停之。
value.en: Even twenty-four rope-boys were denied.
value.literal: When the ministry asked for twenty-four pullers, the edict stopped that as well.

value.zh: 及宣帝，遺詔「子弟群官皆不得謁陵」。
value.en: Emperor Xuan's testament commanded that "sons, younger kin, and all officials must not visit the imperial tombs."
value.literal: Emperor Xuan's testament commanded that "sons, younger kin, and all officials must not visit the imperial tombs."

value.zh: 於是景、文遵旨。
value.en: Sima Shi and Sima Zhao complied.
value.literal: Jing and Wen obeyed that order.

value.zh: 至武帝，猶再謁崇陽陵，一謁峻平陵，然遂不敢謁高原陵，至惠帝復止也。
value.en: Sima Yan alone made limited visits, never to Cao Cao's mound, and Hui abandoned the habit entirely.
value.literal: Emperor Wu still visited Chongyang twice and Junping once, yet never dared approach Gaoling; under Emperor Hui the custom lapsed again.

value.zh: 《五經通義》以為有德則諡善，無德則諡惡，故雖君臣可同。
value.en: "Tongyi of the Five Classics" holds that if one is virtuous, the posthumous title will be good, and if there is no virtue, the posthumous title will be evil, so although the emperor and his ministers can be the same.
value.literal: "Tongyi of the Five Classics" holds that if one is virtuous, the posthumous title will be good, and if there is no virtue, the posthumous title will be evil, so although the emperor and his ministers can be the same.

value.zh: 魏朝初諡''『宣帝為文侯，景王為武侯』''，文王表不宜與二祖同，於是改諡宣文、忠武。
value.en: At the beginning of the Wei Dynasty, the posthumous titles were ""Emperor Xuan was Marquis Wen, and King Jing was Marquis Wu". It was inappropriate for King Wen to have the same title as his second ancestor, so the posthumous titles were changed to Xuanwen and Zhongwu.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Wei Dynasty, the posthumous titles were ""Emperor Xuan was Marquis Wen, and King Jing was Marquis Wu". It was inappropriate for King Wen to have the same title as his second ancestor, so the posthumous titles were changed to Xuanwen and Zhongwu.

value.zh: 至文王受晉王之號，魏帝又追命宣文為宣王，忠武為景王。
value.en: When King Wen received the title of King of Jin, Emperor Wei also appointed Xuanwen as King Xuan and Zhongwu as King Jing.
value.literal: When King Wen received the title of King of Jin, Emperor Wei also appointed Xuanwen as King Xuan and Zhongwu as King Jing.

value.zh: 太康八年十月，太常上諡故太常平陵男郭奕為景侯。
value.en: In the eighth year of Taikang, in October, Taichang was given the posthumous title, so Guo Yi, the man from Pingling, Taichang, was given the title of Marquis of Jing.
value.literal: In the eighth year of Taikang, in October, Taichang was given the posthumous title, so Guo Yi, the man from Pingling, Taichang, was given the title of Marquis of Jing.

value.zh: 有司奏云：「晉受命以來，祖宗號諡群下未有同者，故郭奕為景，與景皇同，不可聽，宜諡曰穆。」
value.en: An official report said: "Since the Jin Dynasty, there has been no one with the same posthumous title for his ancestors. Therefore, Guo Yi is the king of Jing, and he is the same as Emperor Jing. It is not acceptable to listen to him, so it is appropriate to give him the posthumous title Mu."
value.literal: An official report said: "Since the Jin Dynasty, there has been no one with the same posthumous title for his ancestors. Therefore, Guo Yi is the king of Jing, and he is the same as Emperor Jing. It is not acceptable to listen to him, so it is appropriate to give him the posthumous title Mu."

value.zh: 王濟、羊璞等並云：「夫無窮之祚，名諡不一，若皆相避，于制難全。
value.en: Wang Ji, Yang Pu, and the others all said: “In an endless imperial blessing, personal names and posthumous titles are not all the same; if all are mutually avoided, the system is hard to complete.
value.literal: Wang Ji, Yang Pu, and the others all said: “In an endless imperial blessing, personal names and posthumous titles are not all the same; if all are mutually avoided, the system is hard to complete.

value.zh: 如悉不避，復非推崇事尊之禮。
value.en: If none are avoided, that again is not the rite of exalting and serving the honored.
value.literal: If none are avoided, that again is not the rite of exalting and serving the honored.

value.zh: 宜依諱名之義，但及七廟祖宗而已，不及遷毀之廟。」
value.en: It is fitting to follow the meaning of name taboo only as far as the ancestors in the seven temples, and not extend it to temples whose tablets have been moved out or destroyed.”
value.literal: It is fitting to follow the meaning of name taboo only as far as the ancestors in the seven temples, and not extend it to temples whose tablets have been moved out or destroyed.”

value.zh: 成粲、武茂、劉訥並云：「同諡非嫌。
value.en: Cheng Can, Wu Mao and Liu Na all said, "It is not inappropriate to have the same posthumous title.
value.literal: Cheng Can, Wu Mao and Liu Na all said, "It is not inappropriate to have the same posthumous title.

value.zh: 號諡者，國之大典，所以厲時作教，經天人之遠旨也。
value.en: The person with the posthumous title is the grand ceremony of the country, so he teaches in a timely manner and obeys the distant decrees of heaven and man.
value.literal: The person with the posthumous title is the grand ceremony of the country, so he teaches in a timely manner and obeys the distant decrees of heaven and man.

value.zh: 固雖君父，義有所不隆，及在臣子，或以行顯。
value.en: Even though you are a king and father, your righteousness is not upheld, and it may be shown by your actions to your ministers.
value.literal: Even though you are a king and father, your righteousness is not upheld, and it may be shown by your actions to your ministers.

value.zh: 故能使上下邁德，罔有怠荒。
value.en: Therefore, it can bring great virtue to both the superiors and subordinates, without any laziness or neglect.
value.literal: Therefore, it can bring great virtue to both the superiors and subordinates, without any laziness or neglect.

value.zh: 臣願聖世同符堯舜，行周同諡之禮，舍漢魏近制相避之議。」
value.en: I hope that the Holy World will be the same as Yao and Shun, and that the posthumous rites of Zhou Dynasty will be the same, and that the modern system of Han and Wei will be avoided.”
value.literal: I hope that the Holy World will be the same as Yao and Shun, and that the posthumous rites of Zhou Dynasty will be the same, and that the modern system of Han and Wei will be avoided.”

value.zh: 又引周公父子同諡曰文。
value.en: He also cited Zhou Gong and his son as having the same posthumous title.
value.literal: He also cited Zhou Gong and his son as having the same posthumous title.

value.zh: 武帝詔曰：「非言君臣不可同，正以奕諡景不相當耳，宜諡曰簡。」
value.en: Emperor Wu issued an edict: "It is not necessary to say that the emperor and his ministers cannot be the same. Since the posthumous title of Yi is not commensurate with the scenery, it is appropriate to give him the posthumous title of Jian."
value.literal: Emperor Wu issued an edict: "It is not necessary to say that the emperor and his ministers cannot be the same. Since the posthumous title of Yi is not commensurate with the scenery, it is appropriate to give him the posthumous title of Jian."

value.zh: 及太元四年，侍中王欣之表君臣之嫌同諡，尚書奏以欣之言為然。
value.en: In Taiyuan 4, Palace Attendant Wang Xinzhi objected that ruler and minister should not share a posthumous title, and the Masters of Writing endorsed his view.
value.literal: When it came to Taiyuan 4, Palace Attendant Wang Xinzhi memorialized that ruler and minister should avoid sharing the same posthumous title, and the Masters of Writing reported that Xinzhi's statement was correct.

value.zh: 詔可。
value.en: The edict can be issued.
value.literal: The edict can be issued.

value.zh: 樂志下
value.en: Treatise on Music, Part Two
value.literal: Treatise on Music, Part Two

value.zh: 及武帝受禪，乃令傅玄制為二十二篇，亦述以功德代魏。
value.en: After Emperor Wu took the abdicated throne he told Fu Xuan to write twenty-two lyrics chronicling Jin merit supplanting Wei.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted abdication, he ordered Fu Xuan to compose twenty-two pieces, likewise narrating merit and virtue replacing Wei.

value.zh: 改《朱鷺》為《靈之祥》，言宣帝之佐魏，猶虞舜之事堯，既有石瑞之徵，又能用武以誅孟達之逆命也。
value.en: 《Red Egret》 became 《Omen of the Spirits》, likening Sima Yi's service to Wei to Shun serving Yao: stone omens appeared and arms crushed Meng Da's revolt.
value.literal: They changed 《Red Egret》 to 《Auspice of the Numina》, referring to how Emperor Xuan aided Wei as Yu Shun served Yao, having both the omen of stone talisman and the ability to use arms to execute Meng Da's treasonous command.

value.zh: 改《思悲翁》為《宣受命》，言宣帝御諸葛亮，養威重，運神兵，亮震怖而死也。
value.en: 《Thinking of the Old Man》 became 《Xuan Takes the Charge》, describing Sima Yi's stalemate with Zhuge Liang—stored dread majesty, maneuvered subtle hosts—until Zhuge Liang died of shock.
value.literal: They changed 《Thinking of the Old Man》 to 《Xuan Receives the Mandate》, referring to how Emperor Xuan opposed Zhuge Liang, nurtured awe-inspiring weight, deployed spirit-like troops, and Liang trembled with terror and died.

value.zh: 改《艾如張》為《征遼東》，言宣帝陵大海之表，討滅公孫氏而梟其首也。
value.en: 《Spreading Mugwort》 was titled 《The Liaodong Expedition》, for Sima Yi's crossing of the sea, destruction of the Gongsuns, and display of Gongsun Yuan's head.
value.literal: They changed 《Spreading Mugwort》 to 《Campaigning Liaodong》, referring to how Emperor Xuan crossed beyond the great sea, attacked and destroyed the Gongsun clan, and exposed their leader's head.

value.zh: 改《上之回》為《宣輔政》，言宣帝聖道深遠，撥亂反正，網羅文武之才，以定二儀之序也。
value.en: 《Ascending to the Turn》 became 《Xuan Orders the Realm》, praising deep sagely policy that righted disorder and ranked talented civil and martial officers.
value.literal: They changed 《Ascending to the Turn》 to 《Xuan Assists the Government》, referring to how Emperor Xuan's sagely way ran deep, set chaos aright and restored order, netted civil and martial talents, and fixed the pattern of the Two Powers.

value.zh: 改《雍離》為《時運多難》，言宣帝致討吳方，有征無戰也。
value.en: 《Yong Leaves Part》 turned into 《Times of Many Perils》, noting punitive moves toward Wu that ended without pitched battle.
value.literal: They changed 《Yong Leaves Part》 to 《The Age Harrows with Many Hardships》, referring to how Emperor Xuan carried punitive expedition to Wu's territory—campaigns without battle.

value.zh: 改《戰城南》為《景龍飛》，言景帝克明威教，賞順夷逆，隆無疆，崇洪基也。
value.en: 《South of the City We Fight》 became 《Soaring Dragon of Splendor》, celebrating Emperor Jing's awe-education, rewarding the loyal, punishing rebels, widening blessing, and deepening the great base.
value.literal: They changed 《South of the City We Fight》 to 《Scenic Dragon Soars》, referring to how Emperor Jing clarified awesome instruction, rewarded compliance and chastised rebellion, elevated boundlessness, and enlarged the mighty foundation.

value.zh: 改《巫山高》為《平玉衡》，言景帝一萬國之殊風，齊四海之乖心，禮賢養士，而纂洪業也。
value.en: 《Mount Wu Is High》 was renamed 《Trueing the Jade Armillary》, for Emperor Jing's harmonizing every region, aligning distant hearts, honoring worthies, and advancing the great enterprise.
value.literal: They changed 《Mount Wu Is High》 to 《Leveling the Jade Balance》, referring to how Emperor Jing unified the myriad nations' diverse customs, aligned the four seas' contrary hearts, honored the worthy and nurtured knights, and continued the great enterprise.

value.zh: 改《上陵》為《文皇統百揆》，言文帝始統百揆，用人有序，以敷太平之化也。
value.en: 《Ascending the Mausoleum》 became 《Emperor Wen Governs All Bureaus》, because Sima Zhao first superintended every office, ordered appointments, and spread great peace.
value.literal: They changed 《Ascending the Mausoleum》 to 《Emperor Wen Commands All Offices》, referring to how Emperor Wen first presided over all bureaus, employed men in due order, and spread the transforming influence of great peace.

value.zh: 改《將進酒》為《因時運》，言因時運變，聖謀潛施，解長蛇之交，離群桀之党，以武濟文，以邁其德也。
value.en: 《Wine, Advance!》 was titled 《Seizing the Hour》, describing timely stratagem that broke Shu-Wu collusion, shattered rebel cliques, paired arms with culture, and heightened virtue.
value.literal: They changed 《Wine, Advance!》 to 《Riding the Season's Fortune》, referring to how following fortune's seasons the sacred stratagem worked in secret, undid the long-serpent alliance, split the pack of fiends, aided culture with arms, and thereby advanced virtue.

value.zh: 改《有所思》為《惟庸蜀》，言文帝既平萬乘之蜀，封建萬國，復五等之爵也。
value.en: 《I Had Someone in Mind》 became 《That Shu Alone》, for Sima Zhao's reduction of the Shu empire, investiture of countless domains, and revival of the five noble ranks.
value.literal: They changed 《I Had Someone in Mind》 to 《Only That Shu》, referring to how Emperor Wen pacified the Shu host of ten thousand chariots, enfeoffed myriad states, and restored the five grades of nobility.

value.zh: 改《芳樹》為《天序》，言聖皇應曆受禪，弘濟大化，用人各盡其才也。
value.en: 《Fragrant Trees》 turned into 《Heaven's Sequence》, celebrating the sage ruler's calendar-abdication, vast transformation, and each talent fully used.
value.literal: They changed 《Fragrant Trees》 to 《Heaven's Ordering》, referring to how the sage emperor answered the calendar and received abdication, broadly aided great transformation, and employed each man to his full talent.

value.zh: 改《上邪》為《大晉承運期》，言聖皇應籙受圖，化象神明也。
value.en: 《Oh Heaven Above》 became 《Great Jin's Hour》, because the sage sovereign answered the tally-charts and merged his likeness with the divine.
value.literal: They changed 《Oh Heaven Above》 to 《Great Jin Receives the Mandate's Season》, referring to how the sage emperor answered the tallies and received the charts, transforming likeness spirit-like.

value.zh: 改《君馬黃》為《金靈運》，言聖皇踐阼，致敬宗廟，而孝道行於天下也。
value.en: 《Your Horse Is Yellow》 was renamed 《Metal Virtue in Motion》, praising accession, ancestral devotion, and filial teaching across the land.
value.literal: They changed 《Your Horse Is Yellow》 to 《The Metal Essence's Course》, referring to how the sage emperor ascended the throne, paid utmost homage at the ancestral shrine, and filial devotion ran through the realm.

value.zh: 改《雉子班》為《于穆我皇》，言聖皇受禪，德合神明也。
value.en: 《Pheasant Broods》 became 《How Majestic Our King》, for the abdicated accession and virtue mirroring the gods.
value.literal: They changed 《Pheasant Broods》 to 《Oh Solemn Our Sovereign》, referring to how the sage emperor received abdication and virtue matched spirit luminaries.

value.zh: 改《聖人出》為《仲春振旅》，言大晉申文武之教，畋獵以時也。
value.en: 《The Sage Appears》 was titled 《Spring Hunt Drills the Troops》, recording Jin extension of civil-martial instruction and seasonal hunts.
value.literal: They changed 《The Sage Appears》 to 《Second Month Drills the Host》, referring to how Great Jin extended civil and martial teaching and hunted according to season.

value.zh: 改《臨高臺》為《夏苗田》，言大晉畋狩順時，為苗除害也。
value.en: 《From the High Terrace》 became 《Summer Seedling Hunt》, when Jin drove off vermin in accord with the calendar.
value.literal: They changed 《From the High Terrace》 to 《Summer Seedling Hunt》, referring to how Great Jin hunted in accord with season to rid the fields of harm.

value.zh: 改《遠如期》為《仲秋獮田》，言大晉雖有文德，不廢武事，順時以殺伐也。
value.en: 《Far as the Promised Day》 turned into 《Autumn Hunt in Order》, insisting that even with civil splendor Jin still struck punishments on schedule.
value.literal: They changed 《Far as the Promised Day》 to 《Second Month Autumn Hunt》, referring to how Great Jin, though possessing civil virtue, did not neglect martial affairs, following season for punitive strikes.

value.zh: 改《石留》為《順天道》，言仲冬大閱，用武修文，大晉之德配天也。
value.en: 《Stone Stays》 was renamed 《Following Heaven's Road》, for midwinter grand reviews where arms perfected culture and Jin matched heaven.
value.literal: They changed 《Stone Stays》 to 《Obeying Heaven's Way》, referring to how in mid-winter the grand review used arms to cultivate culture, Great Jin's virtue matching heaven.

value.zh: 改《務成》為《唐堯》，言聖皇陟帝位，德化光四表也。
value.en: 《Accomplishing Completion》 became 《Emperor Yao of Tang》, because the sage ruler mounted the throne and edifying virtue lit the four quarters.
value.literal: They changed 《Accomplishing Completion》 to 《Tang Yao》, referring to how the sage emperor ascended the throne of emperor and moral transformation irradiated the four outer regions.

value.zh: 《玄雲》依舊名，言聖皇用人，各盡其材也。
value.en: 《Dark Clouds》 stayed unchanged, depicting every talent placed according to his gifts.
value.literal: 《Dark Clouds》 kept its old name, referring to how the sage emperor employed men, each to his material.

value.zh: 改《黃爵行》為《伯益》，言赤烏銜書，有周以興，今聖皇受命，神雀來也。
value.en: 《Yellow Sparrow March》 became 《Helper Yi》, comparing the crimson crow's writ that launched Zhou to the spirit finches greeting Jin's charge.
value.literal: They changed 《Yellow Sparrow March》 to 《Boy Yi》, referring to how the red crow bore writing—Zhou rose thereby—and now the sage emperor received the mandate and spirit magpies came.

value.zh: 《釣竿》依舊名，言聖皇德配堯舜，又有呂望之佐，濟大功，致太平也。
value.en: 《Fishing Rod》 remained, pairing Jin virtue with Yao-Shun and Lü Wang's aid to finish the great task of peace.
value.literal: 《Fishing Rod》 kept its old name, referring to how the sage emperor's virtue matched Yao and Shun and he also had Lü Wang's assistance to accomplish great work and bring about great peace.

value.zh: 其辭並列之於後雲。
value.en: The texts follow in order.
value.literal: Their lyrics are all listed below.

value.zh: 靈之祥，石瑞章。
value.en: Spirit blessing—stone portents blaze.
value.literal: Auspice of the numina—stone omens bright.

value.zh: 旌金德，出西方。
value.en: Metal virtue revealed, rising from the west.
value.literal: Displaying metal virtue, emerging from the west.

value.zh: 天降命，授宣皇。
value.en: Heaven sent its mandate, granting Emperor Xuan.
value.literal: Heaven dropped the charge, bestowed on Emperor Xuan.

value.zh: 應期運，時龍驤。
value.en: He rides the hour's luck; the dragon rears on high.
value.literal: Answering timely fortune, for the moment the dragon rears.

value.zh: 繼大舜，佐陶唐。
value.en: He follows Great Shun, assists lofty Tang.
value.literal: Continuing great Shun, assisting lofty Tang.

value.zh: 贊武文，建帝綱。
value.en: He upholds civil and martial, sets the royal span.
value.literal: Praising civil and martial, establishing imperial norm.

value.zh: 孟氏叛，據南疆。
value.en: Meng Da rebelled, gripping the southern marches.
value.literal: The Meng clan rebelled, holding the southern frontier.

value.zh: 追有扈，亂五常。
value.en: Like punishing You-Hu, he smashes the five norms.
value.literal: Pursuing the You-Hu, disordering the five constants.

value.zh: 吳寇叛，蜀虜強。
value.en: Wu raiders rise; Shu hosts stay fierce.
value.literal: Wu bandits rebelled; Shu captives strong.

value.zh: 交誓盟，連遐荒。
value.en: They swear dire alliances, chain the far frontiers.
value.literal: Swearing leagues of alliance, linking distant wastes.

value.zh: 宣赫怒，奮鷹揚。
value.en: Xuan vents fierce wrath, lifts wings like hawks.
value.literal: Xuan roused fierce wrath, soaring like the hawk.

value.zh: 震乾威，曜電光。
value.en: He shakes celestial awe, flashes lightning sheen.
value.literal: Shaking heaven's majesty, flashing lightning's gleam.

value.zh: 陵九天，陷石城。
value.en: He climbs the nine tiers, storms Stone Fort hold.
value.literal: Scaling the nine heavens, toppling Stone City.

value.zh: 梟逆命，拯有生。
value.en: He cuts the rebel charge, saves the breathing folk.
value.literal: Beheading the traitor's mandate, saving the living throng.

value.zh: 萬國安，四海寧。
value.en: Ten thousand regions rest; four seas grow calm.
value.literal: Ten thousand lands secure; the four seas at peace.

value.zh: 宣受命
value.en: Xuan Receives the Mandate
value.literal: Xuan Receives the Mandate

value.zh: 宣受命，應天機，風雲時動神龍飛。
value.en: Xuan takes heaven's charge; clouds ride the hour—the dragon lifts.
value.literal: Xuan receives the mandate, answers heaven's instrument; wind and clouds move in season—divine dragon flies.

value.zh: 禦葛亮，鎮雍梁。
value.en: He bars Zhuge Liang, shields Yong and Liang.
value.literal: He fences off Zhuge Liang, guards Yong and Liang.

value.zh: 邊境安，夷夏康。
value.en: Frontiers lock tight; tribes and heartland easy.
value.literal: Borderlands secure; barbarians and Xia at ease.

value.zh: 務節事，勤定傾。
value.en: He trims state affairs, labors to right the leaning throne.
value.literal: He attends to modest duty, toils to steady the tipping scale.

value.zh: 攬英雄，保持盈。
value.en: He collects champions, guards surplus with care.
value.literal: He gathers heroes, holds fullness in care.

value.zh: 深穆穆，赫明明。
value.en: Deep and still, blazingly bright.
value.literal: Profound and solemn, radiant and bright.

value.zh: 沖而泰，天之經。
value.en: Supple and still—the warp of heaven.
value.literal: Subtle and tranquil—heaven's constant warp.

value.zh: 養威重，運神兵。
value.en: He stores dread weight, drives spirit-like hosts.
value.literal: He nurtures dread majesty, wields spirit-like troops.

value.zh: 亮乃震斃，天下安寧。
value.en: Liang dies of dread; the realm lies quiet.
value.literal: Liang then quaked and perished; all under heaven secure and still.

value.zh: 征遼東，敵失據，威靈邁日域。
value.en: The Liaodong war—foes lose footing; awe crosses the solar sphere.
value.literal: Campaigning Liaodong—foe loses foothold; dread majesty crosses the sun's realm.

value.zh: 公孫既授首，群逆破膽，咸震怖。
value.en: Gongsun Yuan loses his head; rebels melt with fear.
value.literal: Gongsun beheaded; crowd of rebels' gall melts—all shake in terror.

value.zh: 朔北回應，海表景附。
value.en: The northern wastes answer; overseas shores cling like shadows.
value.literal: The northern north responds; beyond the seas gaze and cling like shadows.

value.zh: 武功赫赫，德雲布。
value.en: His martial glory blazes; kindness rains like clouds.
value.literal: Martial prowess shines terrifying; virtue spreads like clouds.

value.zh: 宣輔政
value.en: Xuan Assists the Government
value.literal: Xuan Assists the Government

value.zh: 宣皇輔政，聖烈深。
value.en: The Xuan emperor steered the realm; sacred power ran profound.
value.literal: Emperor Xuan aids governance; sagely merit runs deep.

value.zh: 撥亂反正，順天心。
value.en: He straightened the turmoil and matched heaven's mind.
value.literal: He sets chaos aright and restores orthodoxy; he accords with heaven's heart.

value.zh: 網羅文武才，慎厥所生。
value.en: He gathered civil and martial talent and fostered each calling.
value.literal: He nets civil and martial talents; cautiously he nurtures what they bear.

value.zh: 所生賢，遺教施。
value.en: Those nurtured proved worthy; his legacy spread as doctrine.
value.literal: What they bear proves worthy; his bequeathed teaching spreads.

value.zh: 安上治民，化風移。
value.en: He steadied ruler and folk and shifted customs through reform.
value.literal: He settles superiors and governs the people; transforming customs shift.

value.zh: 肇創帝基，洪業垂。
value.en: He founded the dynastic base and hung the great enterprise forth.
value.literal: He begins creation of the imperial foundation; vast enterprise hangs down.

value.zh: 于鑠明明，時赫戲。
value.en: How radiant his gleam, how fierce his shining play.
value.literal: Oh, blaze so bright, splendid and shining, momentous display.

value.zh: 功濟萬世，定二儀。
value.en: His work aids endless ages; he set heaven and earth aright.
value.literal: Merit aids ten thousand generations; he fixes the Two Powers.

value.zh: 定二儀，雲行雨施，海外風馳。
value.en: Heaven and earth aligned: clouds rode, rain fell, winds raced overseas.
value.literal: Fixing the Two Powers: clouds move and rain falls; beyond the seas winds gallop.

value.zh: 時運多難，道教痡。
value.en: Hard times exhausted the Way; instruction grew thin.
value.literal: The age harrows with many hardships; the Way's teaching grows weary.

value.zh: 天地變化，有盈虛。
value.en: Sky and soil alternate between wax and wane.
value.literal: Heaven and earth alter and shift; there is fullness and emptiness.

value.zh: 蠢爾吳蠻，武視江湖。
value.en: Those Wu savages eyed the rivers with martial greed.
value.literal: You foolish Wu barbarians--martially you gaze on rivers and lakes.

value.zh: 我皇赫斯，致天誅。
value.en: Our sovereign rose in wrath to wield heaven's scourge.
value.literal: Our emperor awesome thus--brings heaven's punishment upon you.

value.zh: 有征無戰，弭其圖。
value.en: Campaigns ended without pitched battle; their schemes collapsed.
value.literal: Where there is campaign there is no battle; your plots are stilled.

value.zh: 天威橫被，廓東隅。
value.en: Heaven's awe swept outward and cleared the eastern march.
value.literal: Heaven's majesty spreads horizontally; opens the eastern corner.

value.zh: 《書》曰：「唐虞稽古，建官惟百。」
value.en: The Book of Documents says: "When Tang and Yu looked back to antiquity, they created no more than a hundred offices."
value.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Tang and Yu examined antiquity; they established offices numbering only one hundred."

value.zh: 所以獎導民萌，裁成庶政。
value.en: That was how they encouraged the people and gave shape to the affairs of state.
value.literal: By this means they encouraged and guided the common people, and brought order to every branch of government.

value.zh: 《易》曰：「天垂象，聖人則之。」
value.en: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven displays signs; the sage patterns himself on them."
value.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven hangs forth images; the sage takes them as his model."

value.zh: 執法在南宮之右，上相處端門之外，而鳥龍居位，雲火垂名，前史詳之，其以尚矣。
value.en: Justice lay to the right of the Southern Palace; the chief minister waited beyond the Duan Gate; bird and dragon offices held rank with cloud and fire as their emblems—prior histories lay it out clearly, and the grandeur speaks for itself.
value.literal: Law sat to the right of the Southern Palace; the chief minister took station beyond the Duan Gate; the Bird and Dragon offices held their posts, cloud and fire lending their names—earlier histories spell this out in detail, and the dignity of it is plain.

value.zh: 黃帝置三公之秩，以親黎元，少昊配九扈之名，以為農正，命重黎於天地，詔融冥於水火，則可得而言焉。
value.en: The Yellow Emperor created the Three Dukes to draw near to the people; Shaohao aligned the Nine Hu titles with agricultural oversight; Chong and Li received Heaven and Earth; Zhu Rong and Ming received fire and water—and such patterns can be put into words.
value.literal: The Yellow Emperor instituted the ranks of the Three Dukes to stay close to the black-haired masses; Shaohao paired the Nine Hu bird-names with the office of director of agriculture; Chong and Li were charged with Heaven and Earth; Zhu Rong and Ming were charged with fire and water—these arrangements can indeed be described.

value.zh: 伊尹曰：「三公調陰陽，九卿通寒暑，大夫知人事，列士去其私。」
value.en: Yi Yin said: "The Three Dukes harmonize yin and yang; the Nine Ministers track the seasons; grand officers attend to human affairs; ranked officers put private interest aside."
value.literal: Yi Yin said: "The Three Dukes harmonize yin and yang; the Nine Ministers watch cold and heat; grand officers understand human affairs; ranked officers rid themselves of selfishness."

value.zh: 而成湯居亳，初置二相，以伊尹、仲虺為之，凡厥樞會，仰承君命。
value.en: When Tang of Shang made Bo his seat, he first set up two chancellors—Yi Yin and Zhong Hui—and on every pivot they carried out the sovereign's will.
value.literal: When Cheng Tang ruled from Bo, he first created two chancellors and appointed Yi Yin and Zhong Hui to them; on every critical matter they looked upward to receive the ruler's commands.

value.zh: 總及周武下車，成康垂則，六卿分職，二公弘化，咸樹司存，各題標準，苟非其道，人弗虛榮。
value.en: Under King Wu and the models left by Cheng and Kang, the Six Ministers split the labor, the Two Dukes carried royal influence abroad, every bureau had its charter, and no one claimed idle honors without the right conduct.
value.literal: Altogether, when King Wu of Zhou stepped down from his chariot to rule, Cheng and Kang handed down norms; the Six Ministers divided duties; the Two Dukes spread transformation; each office kept its place and measure; if it were not the proper Way, people did not vainly seek glory.

value.zh: 貽厥孫謀，其固本也如此。
value.en: They anchored the dynasty by planning for generations yet unborn.
value.literal: They left plans for their descendants; thus they secured the foundation.

value.zh: 及秦變周官，漢遵嬴舊，或隨時適用，或因務遷革，霸王之典，義在於斯，既獲厥安，所謂得其時制者也。
value.en: Qin refashioned Zhou's bureaucracy; Han largely kept Qin's frame while tweaking it for the moment—the logic of strong rule was there—and stability meant institutions matched their age.
value.literal: When Qin altered the Zhou offices and Han followed the Ying-clan precedent, sometimes adapting to the times, sometimes shifting with practical needs—the norms of hegemons and kings lay herein; once stability was gained, this is what is called obtaining timely institutions.

value.zh: 四征興於漢代，四安起于魏初，四鎮通於柔遠，四平止於喪亂，其渡遼、淩江，輕車、強弩，式揚遐外，用表攻伐，興而復毀，厥號彌繁。
value.en: Han invented the Four Expeditions; Wei at its outset the Four Pacifications; Four Garrisons stretched toward distant peoples; Four Peace posts vanished when chaos returned. Epithets like Crossing-the-Liao, River-Fording, light chariot, and strong crossbow brandished force beyond the borders for campaigns—created, scrapped, then multiplied until the catalogue grew tangled.
value.literal: The Four Expeditions arose in Han; the Four Pacifications began at the start of Wei; the Four Garrisons reached outward to soothe the distant; the Four Peace offices ended with turmoil and disorder; as for Crossing-the-Liao, River-Fording, light chariot, and strong crossbow—they displayed might afar and signaled campaigns—raised up and then abolished, their titles grew ever more numerous.

value.zh: 及當塗得志，克平諸夏，初有軍師祭酒，參掌戎律。
value.en: Once the Cao regime triumphed and pacified the heartland, it introduced the army adviser libationer to share oversight of military law.
value.literal: When the house at Dangtu achieved its ambition and subdued the Central Plain, there first appeared the army adviser libationer, who jointly handled military regulations.

value.zh: 建安十三年，罷漢台司，更置丞相，而以曹公居之，用兼端揆。
value.en: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an (208), the Han ministerial posts were abolished, the chancellorship was reinstated, and Lord Cao held it, thereby combining the highest civil authority.
value.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an, the Han terrace ministers were abolished; the chancellor was reinstated, and Lord Cao held it, thereby combining the highest civil authority.

value.zh: 孫吳、劉蜀，多依漢制，雖復臨時命氏，而無忝舊章。
value.en: Wu and Shu largely kept Han models; occasional improvised titles notwithstanding, they stayed within the classical mold.
value.literal: Eastern Wu and Liu Bei's Shu largely followed Han institutions; though they sometimes improvised titles on the spot, they did not shame the old statutes.

value.zh: 世祖武皇帝即位之初，以安平王孚為太宰，鄭沖為太傅，王祥為太保，司馬望為太尉，何曾為司徒，荀顗為司空，石苞為大司馬，陳騫為大將軍，世所謂八公同辰，攀雲附翼者也。
value.en: At his accession, Emperor Wu named Sima Fu Grand Preceptor, Zheng Chong Grand Tutor, Wang Xiang Grand Guardian, Sima Wang Minister of War, He Zeng Minister of Education, Xun Yi Minister of Works, Shi Bao Grand Marshal, and Chen Qian Grand General—the storied eight dukes of a single hour, men who rose by riding imperial favor.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu the Shizu first ascended the throne, he appointed Prince Fu of Anping as Grand Preceptor, Zheng Chong as Grand Tutor, Wang Xiang as Grand Guardian, Sima Wang as Minister of War, He Zeng as Minister of Education, Xun Yi as Minister of Works, Shi Bao as Grand Marshal, and Chen Qian as Grand General—what the age called the eight dukes sharing one hour, climbing clouds and attaching wings.

value.zh: 若乃成乎棟宇，非一枝之勢；
value.en: Raising the whole hall takes more than one timber;
value.literal: As for completing roof-beams and rafters—it is not the strength of a single branch;

value.zh: 處乎經綸，稱萬夫之敵。
value.en: true stewardship of the realm earns the title match for ten thousand.
value.literal: to dwell in ordering the realm is to be called a match for ten thousand men.

value.zh: 或牽羊以葉於夢，或垂釣以申其道，或空桑以獻其術，或操版以啟其心。
value.en: Some arrived through dreams of sheep and grain; some through fishing metaphors; some from humble soil with a craft to sell; some by presenting the royal tablet and winning trust.
value.literal: Some led sheep and answered a leaf in a dream; some angled with a hook to proclaim their Way; some offered their arts from an empty mulberry; some grasped the tablet to open the ruler's mind.

value.zh: 臥龍飛鴻，方金擬璧，秦奚、鄭產，楚材晉用，斯亦曩時之良具，其又昭彰者焉。
value.en: Hidden dragons and soaring swans, talents weighed like gold against jade—Qin Xi, Zheng Chan, and Chu talent employed by Jin: these too were fine instruments of former times, and no less manifest.
value.literal: The sleeping dragon, the soaring wild goose—square metal compared to round jade; the shepherd of Qin, the prodigy of Zheng; Chu talent employed by Jin—these too were fine instruments of former times, and no less manifest.

value.zh: 宣王既誅曹爽，政由己出，網羅英俊，以備天官。
value.en: After Sima Yi eliminated Cao Shuang, he ruled in his own name and stocked every court post with talent.
value.literal: Once Prince Xuan had executed Cao Shuang, government proceeded from himself alone; he gathered capable men to fill the celestial offices.

value.zh: 及蘭卿受羈，貴公顯戮，雖復策名魏氏，而乃心皇晉。
value.en: When fine officers were seized and great nobles died in public execution, names might still stand with Wei but hearts had already turned to Jin.
value.literal: When worthy ministers were placed under restraint and eminent dukes suffered public execution—though they still bore registration under the Wei, their hearts were with the august Jin.

value.zh: 及文王纂業，初啟晉台，始置二衛，有前驅養由之弩；
value.en: When Sima Zhao extended the family work and founded the Jin apparatus, he created the Two Guards with vanguard crossbows worthy of Yang Youji.
value.literal: When King Wen continued the enterprise and first opened the Jin terrace, he began setting up the Two Guards, including front-vanguard crossbows like Yang Youji's.

value.zh: 及設三部，有熊渠佽飛之眾。
value.en: When the Three Corps were established, there were masses like those of Xiong Qu and Ci Fei.
value.literal: When the Three Departments were established, there were masses like the royal swimmers of Xiong Qu.

value.zh: 是以武帝龍飛，乘茲奮翼，猶武王以周之十亂而理殷民者也。
value.en: Thus Emperor Wu's rise—vaulting on these preparations—matched King Wu deploying his ten able assistants to rule the former Shang subjects.
value.literal: Therefore when Emperor Wu ascended like a dragon, riding this to beat his wings, it was like King Wu of Zhou using the Zhou's ten ministers to govern the Yin people.

value.zh: 是以泰始盡于太康，喬柯茂葉，來居斯位；
value.en: From the Taishi era through Taikang, imposing figures filled those ranks;
value.literal: Thus from Taishi through Taikang, tall trees with lush foliage came to occupy these posts;

value.zh: 自太興訖於建元，南金北銑，用處茲秩。
value.en: from Daxing to Jianyuan, the finest metal south and north filled those offices.
value.literal: from Daxing down to Jianyuan, southern gold and northern ore were employed in these ranks.

value.zh: 雖未擬乎夔拊龍言，天工人代，亦庶幾乎任官惟賢，蒞事惟能者也。
value.en: They fell short of the sage-kings' marriage of Heaven's work to human agency, yet they neared the ideal: office by virtue, tasks by competence.
value.literal: Though they did not equal Kui's drumming and Long's pronouncements—Heaven's work and man's substitute—they approximated appoint officials only for worth, approach affairs only by ability.

value.zh: 四征鎮安平加大將軍不開府、持節都督者，品秩第二，置參佐吏卒，幕府兵騎如常都督制，唯朝會祿賜從二品將軍之例。
value.en: Expeditionary grand generals with credentials but no mansion ranked second; staffs matched normal commanders; court pay followed second-grade rules.
value.literal: Four expeditions, garrisons, pacification, peace with added grand general title, without headquarters, credential-bearing commanders were grade second; staff and runners followed ordinary commander rules; only court assembly stipends followed second-grade general precedent.

value.zh: 然則持節、都督無定員，前漢遣使始有持節。
value.en: Area commanders had no fixed headcount; Former Han invented credential-bearing missions.
value.literal: Thus credential-bearing commanders had no fixed quota; Former Han first had credential-bearing envoys.

value.zh: 光武建武初，征伐四方，始權時置督軍御史，事竟罷。
value.en: Guangwu's early campaigns used temporary army censors, then disbanded them.
value.literal: At the start of Guangwu's Jianwu, campaigning in four directions, temporary army-supervising censors were first set up; when the task ended they were abolished.

value.zh: 建安中，魏武為相，始遣大將軍督之。
value.en: Mid-Jian'an Cao Cao as chancellor began assigning grand generals to oversee armies.
value.literal: In Jian'an, Wei Wu as chancellor first dispatched grand generals to supervise.

value.zh: 二十一年，征孫權還，夏侯惇督二十六軍是也。
value.en: In 216, returning from the campaign against Sun Quan, Xiahou Dun supervised twenty-six armies; this is an instance.
value.literal: In the twenty-first year, returning from campaigning against Sun Quan, Xiahou Dun supervised twenty-six armies—this is an instance.

value.zh: 魏文帝黃初三年，始置都督諸州軍事，或領刺史。
value.en: 222 CE introduced provincial military commanders, often doubling as governors.
value.literal: In Wei Wendi's third Huangchu year, commanders-in-chief of military affairs of various provinces were first established; some concurrently held inspector posts.

value.zh: 又上軍大將軍曹真都督中外諸軍事、假黃鉞，則總統內外諸軍矣。
value.en: Cao Zhen as senior grand general with the golden axe commanded every army at court and frontier.
value.literal: Moreover Upper-army Grand General Cao Zhen commanded inner and outer armies with borrowed yellow axe—thus he commanded all armies within and without.

value.zh: 魏明帝太和四年秋，宣帝征蜀，加號大都督。
value.en: In the autumn of Emperor Ming of Wei's fourth Taihe year, Prince Xuan campaigned against Shu and added the title supreme commander.
value.literal: Autumn of Wei Mingdi's fourth Taihe year, Prince Xuan campaigned against Shu and added the title supreme commander.

value.zh: 高貴鄉公正元二年，文帝都督中外諸軍，尋加大都督。
value.en: 254 CE Sima Zhao commanded all forces, then took supreme commander.
value.literal: In Gaoguixiang Duke's second Zhenyuan year, Prince Wen commanded inner and outer armies; soon after he added supreme commander.

value.zh: 及晉受禪，都督諸軍為上，臨諸軍次之，督諸軍為下；
value.en: Jin ranked titles: commander-in-chief highest, overseer next, supervisor lowest;
value.literal: When Jin received abdication, commander-in-chief of various armies was highest, overseeing various armies next, supervising various armies lowest;

value.zh: 使持節為上，持節次之，假節為下。
value.en: Full powers ranked above ordinary credential, which ranked above borrowed.
value.literal: Bearer of full powers highest, credential-holder next, borrowed credential lowest.

value.zh: 使持節得殺二千石以下；
value.en: Full powers allowed executing officials through two-thousand-shi rank;
value.literal: Bearer of full powers could execute officials down to two thousand shi;

value.zh: 持節殺無官位人，若軍事，得與使持節同；
value.en: Ordinary credentials covered commoners; in war matched full powers;
value.literal: credential-holder could kill persons without office rank; in military matters could match bearer of full powers;

value.zh: 假節唯軍事得殺犯軍令者。
value.en: Borrowed credentials executed only military offenders.
value.literal: borrowed credential only in military affairs could kill violators of military orders.

value.zh: 江左以來，都督中外尤重，唯王導等權重者乃居之。
value.en: South of the river, supreme command rarely fell except to figures as powerful as Wang Dao.
value.literal: Since the Jiang left, commander-in-chief of inner and outer has been especially weighty; only men of heavy authority like Wang Dao have held it.

value.zh: 昔者先王量地以制邑，度地以居民，因三才以節其務，敬四序以成其業，觀其謠俗而正其紀綱。
value.en: The kings of old sized out territory to lay out towns, reckoned acreage to house the people, tuned their duties to the triad of Heaven, earth, and mankind, kept faith with the turning year to finish each season's work, and read popular sentiment so they could straighten what statute and custom required.
value.literal: In antiquity the former kings measured land to regulate settlements, surveyed land to settle the people, guided their tasks according to the three powers (Heaven, Earth, and Man), honored the four seasons to complete their undertakings, and inspected local songs and customs to set right law and discipline.

value.zh: 勖農桑之本，通魚鹽之利，登良山而采符玉，泛瀛海而罩珠璣。
value.en: They promoted tillage and silk as the economy's foundation, extended trade in fish and salt, scaled high hills for ritual jade, and crossed the deep sea to harvest pearls.
value.literal: They urged the root of farming and sericulture, opened access to the profit of fish and salt, climbed worthy hills to gather tally-jade, and sailed the Eastern Sea to seine pearls and precious beads.

value.zh: 日中為市，總天下之隸，先諸布帛，繼以貨泉，貿遷有無，各得其所。
value.en: When the sun stood at the meridian they opened the mart, drawing workers from across the land—first with bolts of cloth, then with coined cash—swapping abundance for scarcity until buyer and seller were matched.
value.literal: They held market at midday, assembling all the laborers of the realm; first came cloth and silk, then currency; they traded surplus for want so that each found his proper place.

value.zh: 《周禮》，正月始和，乃布教于象魏。
value.en: The Zhouli records that with the new year's first month they proclaimed the royal teachings beneath the watch-towers flanking the palace gate.
value.literal: The Rites of Zhou says: In the first month, when harmony begins, they promulgated instruction at the palace gate-towers (xiangwei).

value.zh: 若乃一夫之士，十畝之宅，三日之徭，九均之賦，施陽禮以興其讓，命春社以勖其耕。
value.en: Each farmer had his plot and homestead, a short stint of labor service, and the graded land tax; ritual taught humility, and the spring communal feast kept everyone at the plough.
value.literal: Where one husbandman held his allotment, a homestead of ten mu, three days of corvée, and the ninefold equitable levy, they applied the 'yang' rites to encourage yielding deference and ordered the spring she sacrifice to spur plowing.

value.zh: 天之所貴者人也，明之所求者學也，治《經》入官，則君子之道焉。
value.en: Heaven prizes humanity; good government prizes scholarship; the path of the junzi runs through the canon and into service.
value.literal: What Heaven esteems is human beings; what enlightened rule seeks is learning; mastering the Classics and entering office—that is the way of the gentleman.

value.zh: 《詩》曰：「三之日於耜，四之日舉趾。」
value.en: The Odes says: 'On the third month they sharpen the plough-shares; on the fourth month they raise their feet [to walk to the fields].'
value.literal: The Odes says: 'On the third month they sharpen the plough-shares; on the fourth month they raise their feet [to walk to the fields].'

value.zh: 是以農官澤虞，各有攸次，父兄之習，不玩而成，十五從務，始勝衣服，鄉無遊手，邑不廢時，所謂厥初生民，各從其事者也。
value.en: Hence field overseers and marsh wardens stood in fixed posts; household instruction hardened young hands without play; at fifteen youths took up work and adult clothes; villages held no loafers and towns lost no farming window—that was the world in which, as the ode says, each newborn generation stuck to its calling.
value.literal: Therefore the agricultural and forestry officials each held his station; the customs of fathers and elders were perfected without idle amusement; at fifteen they undertook labor and first wore full adult dress; in the hamlets none wandered idle, in the towns the seasons were not wasted—this is what is meant by 'when the people first arose, each followed his proper task.'

value.zh: 是以太公通市井之貨，以致齊國之強；
value.en: That is how Jiang Taigong turned ward and marketplace into strength for Qi.
value.literal: Thus the Grand Duke opened the circulation of market goods and thereby brought strength to the state of Qi.

value.zh: 鴟夷善發斂之居，以盛中陶之業。
value.en: Fan Li, styled Lord Chiyi, knew how to marshal stores and levies, and so he built up the great pottery workshops of the interior.
value.literal: Lord Chiyi excelled at the depots for fiscal collection; thereby he magnified the pottery industry of the central heartland.

value.zh: 昔在金天，勤於民事，命春鳸以耕稼，召夏鳸以耘鋤，秋鳸所以收斂，冬鳸于焉蓋藏。
value.en: Long ago, under Jin Tian, he was diligent in the people's tasks: he appointed the spring bird-officer for plowing and sowing, summoned the summer bird-officer for weeding and hoeing, used the autumn bird-officer for gathering the harvest, and assigned the winter bird-officer for covering and storing grain.
value.literal: Long ago, in the reign associated with Jin Tian, he was diligent in the people's tasks: he appointed the spring bird-officer for plowing and sowing, summoned the summer bird-officer for weeding and hoeing, relied on the autumn bird-officer for gathering the harvest, and assigned the winter bird-officer for laying grain by.

value.zh: 《書》曰：「曆象日月星辰，敬授民時。」
value.en: The Documents says: 'We calculated and aligned the sun, moon, and stars, and reverently gave the people their seasons.'
value.literal: The Documents says: 'We calculated and aligned the sun, moon, and stars, and reverently gave the people their seasons.'

value.zh: 傳曰：「禹稷躬稼而有天下。」
value.en: The tradition says: 'Yu and Hou Ji personally farmed and thereby gained the realm.'
value.literal: The tradition says: 'Yu and Hou Ji personally farmed and thereby gained the realm.'

value.zh: 若乃九土既敷，四民承范，東吳有齒角之饒，西蜀有丹沙之富，兗豫漆絲之廥，燕齊怪石之府，秦邠旄羽，迥帶琅玕，荊郢桂林，旁通竹箭，江幹橘柚，河外舟車，遼西旃罽之鄉，蔥右蒲梢之駿，殖物怪錯，於何不有。
value.en: Once the nine domains were laid out and the four classes received their models, eastern Wu had abundance of ivory and horn, western Shu had cinnabar wealth, Yan and Yu stored lacquer and silk, Yan and Qi were treasuries of strange stone, Qin and Bin offered yak tails and feathers strung with carnelian, Jing, Ying, and Guilin connected bamboo arrows, riverbanks grew oranges and pomelos, beyond the Yellow River ran boats and carts, Liaoxi was a land of felts and rugs, and west of the Cong ranges came Pu-shao steeds—products multiplied in bewildering variety; what was there that could not be found?
value.literal: When the nine provinces had been laid out and the four peoples received their models, eastern Wu had abundance in ivory and horn, western Shu hoarded cinnabar, Yan and Henan barns brimmed with lacquer and silk, Yan and Qi quarried strange stones, Qin and Bin offered yak tails and kingfisher feathers strung with carnelian, Jing, Ying, and Guilin shipped bamboo arrows, river terraces grew oranges and pomelos, beyond the Yellow River ran boats and carts, Liaoxi was home to felts and rugs, and past the Cong ranges came the famed Pu-shao horses—products multiplied bewilderingly; what was there that could not be found?

value.zh: 若乃上法星象，下料無外，因天地之利，而總山海之饒，百畝之田，十一而稅，九年躬稼，而有三年之蓄，可以長孺齒，可以養耆年。
value.en: Taking cues from the sky and leaving no acre unmeasured on earth, pooling hill and sea wealth, titheing one tenth off each hundred-mu farm, and insisting that nine harvest years include three years of reserves—that was how children grew strong and elders were fed.
value.literal: When they took pattern from the stars above and omitted nothing in surveying below, relying on heaven-and-earth profit and gathering the bounty of mountains and seas, for fields of one hundred mu they levied one part in ten; after nine years of the ruler personally farming they laid up three years' surplus—thereby they could nurture the young and sustain the aged.

value.zh: 因乎人民，用之邦國，宮室有度，旗章有序。
value.en: Carried into hamlet and kingdom, it fixed how high halls might rise and how banners should march in order.
value.literal: Applied among the people and deployed in the feudal states, palace chambers kept their degrees of rank, flags and emblems kept their proper sequence.

value.zh: 朝聘自其儀，宴饗由其制，家殷國阜，遠至邇安。
value.en: Embassies and banquets each had rule-books; wealth filled granaries while neighbors stayed calm.
value.literal: Court audiences and diplomatic missions followed their ritual forms; feasts and communal drinks followed their regulations; households grew rich and the state prosperous, the distant submitted and the near rested secure.

value.zh: 救水旱之災，恤寰瀛之弊，然後王之常膳，乃間笙鏞。
value.en: They drained floods, eased drought, and patched every coastland hurt by scarcity—only then did the throne dine with leisure enough to hear bronze bells.
value.literal: They relieved flood and drought disasters and aided distress throughout the realm; only after that did the king's ordinary meals occasionally include the music of mouth organs and bells.

value.zh: 商周之興，用此道也。
value.en: Shang and Zhou rose by walking this same road.
value.literal: The rise of Shang and Zhou relied on this approach.

value.zh: 辛紂暴虐，玩其經費，金鏤傾宮，廣延百里，玉飾鹿臺，崇高千仞，宮中九市，各有女司。
value.en: King Zhou of Shang (Di Xin) wrecked the treasury through cruelty—gold sheathing for the tilted palace over endless leagues, jade facing for Deer Terrace up sheer cliffs, and nine separate markets inside the palace, each run by female clerks.
value.literal: Xin Zhou was cruel and violent, squandering resources: the tilted palace was overlaid with gold and stretched a hundred li; the Deer Terrace was faced with jade and rose a thousand ren; inside the palace stood nine markets, each supervised by women.

value.zh: 厚賦以實鹿臺之錢，大斂以增钜橋之粟，多發妖冶以充傾宮之麗，廣收珍玩以備沙丘之遊。
value.en: Extortion stacked bronze at Deer Terrace, bulk grain at Juqiao, concubines for the leaning halls, and curios for the revels at Sand Dunes.
value.literal: Heavy levies filled the coin stored at Deer Terrace; vast extractions swelled the grain at Great Bridge Granary; they collected hosts of seductive women to pack the tilted palace with beauty, and amassed rare treasures to supply the revels at Sand Dunes.

value.zh: 懸肉成林，積醪為沼，使男女裸體相逐於其間，伏詣酒池中牛飲者三千餘人，宮中以錦綺為席，綾紈為薦。
value.en: Carcasses hung like a forest, wine pooled like a pond; stripped revelers chased one another while thousands flopped at the pool's lip and sucked wine like oxen; chambers were carpeted in brocade and padded with figured silk.
value.literal: They hung meat until it formed a forest and piled ale until it became a marsh; they made men and women chase one another naked within them; more than three thousand people lay prone along the ale pool and drank like cattle; inside the palace they used damask for mats and fine silk for cushions.

value.zh: 及周王誅紂，肅拜殷墟，乃盡振鹿財，並頒橋粟，上天降休，殷人大喜。
value.en: When King Wu smote the Shang king he emptied the Deer Terrace vaults, threw open Juqiao's granaries, and the conquered capital hailed heaven's mercy.
value.literal: When the king of Zhou punished Zhou of Shang and reverently bowed amid the ruins of Yin, he shook out everything hoarded at Deer Terrace and distributed all the grain from Bridge Granary; Heaven sent its blessing, and the Yin people rejoiced greatly.

value.zh: 王赧云季，徙都西周，九鼎淪沒，二南堙盡，貸于百姓，無以償之，乃上層臺以避其責，周人謂王所居為逃責臺者也。
value.en: King Nan's late reign shifted the court west, lost the cauldrons, silenced the southern hymns, borrowed until bankruptcy, and hid on a platform locals mocked as the terrace for outrunning debt.
value.literal: In the closing years of King Nan he moved the capital to western Zhou; the Nine Tripods sank from sight and the 'two southern' odes fell silent; he borrowed from the hundred surnames and could not repay, so he climbed a high terrace to dodge his creditors—the Zhou people called the king's residence the Debt-Fleeing Terrace.

value.zh: 昔周姬公制以六典，職方陳其九貢，頒財內府，永為不刊。
value.en: Formerly the Duke of Zhou framed the six canons; the Office of Regions set out the nine tribute items; revenue entered the inner treasury and remained an unchanging statute.
value.literal: Formerly the Duke of Zhou framed the six canons; the Office of Regions listed the nine tribute items; revenue entered the inner treasury and remained an unchanging statute.

value.zh: 及刑政陵夷，菁茅罕至，魯侯初踐畝之稅，秦君收太半之入，前王之範，靡有孑遺。
value.en: As government frayed, ritual bundles of thatch grew rare; Lu pioneered the acre tax, Qin seized over half the crop, and ancient fiscal norms vanished.
value.literal: When punishments and government slackened, fine tribute grass seldom arrived; the lord of Lu first trod the tax on field yield; the lord of Qin took more than half the harvest; the models of former kings hardly survived.

value.zh: 史臣曰：班固為《殖貨志》，自三代至王莽之誅，網羅前載，其文詳悉。
value.en: The editors comment: Ban Gu's 'Huozhi zhi' runs from the Xia-Shang-Zhou age to Wang Mang's fall, netting prior sources in exhaustive detail.
value.literal: The historiographer says: Ban Gu composed the 'Treatise on Increasing Wealth,' spanning from the Three Dynasties down to the execution of Wang Mang; it gathers earlier records and its text is thorough.

value.zh: 嘉平四年，關中饑，宣帝表徙冀州農夫五千人佃上邽，興京兆、天水、南安鹽池，以益軍實。
value.en: In the fourth year of Jiaping, a Guanzhong famine drew Sima Yi’s memorial: shift five thousand Ji farmers to Shanggui and work the Jingzhao, Tianshui, and Nan’an brine pans for army stores.
value.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaping, when Guanzhong suffered famine, Emperor Xuan memorialized to move five thousand farmers from Ji Province to colonize Shanggui and to develop the salt pools of Jingzhao, Tianshui, and Nan’an in order to enlarge military stores.

value.zh: 青龍元年，開成國渠自陳倉至槐里；
value.en: In the first year of Qinglong, they cut the Chengguo Canal between Chencang and Huaili.
value.literal: In the first year of Qinglong, they opened the Chengguo Canal from Chencang to Huaili;

value.zh: 築臨晉陂，引汧洛溉舄鹵之地三千餘頃，國以充實焉，
value.en: The Linjin barrage steered the Qian and Luo onto thirty thousand acres of salty flats until the exchequer filled.
value.literal: they built the Linjin weir, drew the Qian and Luo to irrigate more than three thousand qing of alkaline soil, and the state grew ample thereby.

value.zh: 正始四年，宣帝又督諸軍伐吳將諸葛恪，焚其積聚，恪棄城遁走。
value.en: In the fourth year of Zhengshi, Sima Yi next led the strike on Zhuge Ke—torched Wu supplies and drove Ke from his walls.
value.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengshi, Emperor Xuan again supervised the various armies in attacking Wu general Zhuge Ke, burned Ke's stockpiled grain, and Ke abandoned the city and fled.

value.zh: 帝因欲廣田積穀，為兼併之計，乃使鄧艾行陳、項以東，至壽春地。
value.en: Wishing to broaden fields and store grain for a strategy of piecemeal annexation, the emperor sent Deng Ai to survey east from Chen and Xiang as far as the Shouchun region.
value.literal: The emperor therefore wished to broaden fields and pile grain for a strategy of piecemeal annexation, and sent Deng Ai to survey east from Chen and Xiang as far as the Shouchun region.

value.zh: 艾以為田良水少，不足以盡地利，宜開河渠，可以大積軍糧，又通運漕之道。
value.en: Deng Ai held that the soil was good but water scarce, not enough to exhaust the land's potential, and that rivers and canals should be opened to stockpile army grain in quantity and also to connect transport routes.
value.literal: Ai held that the soil was good but water scarce—not enough to exhaust the land's potential—and that rivers and canals should be opened to stockpile army grain in quantity and also link transport routes.

value.zh: 乃著《濟河論》以喻其指。
value.en: He framed the argument in his 'Discourse on Channeling the Ji.'
value.literal: He therefore composed the 'Treatise on the Ji River' to explain his meaning.

value.zh: 又以為昔破黃巾，因為屯田，積穀許都，以制四方。
