value.en: He also argued that when the Yellow Turbans were crushed in former times, agricultural colonies were founded and grain piled at Xu so as to control the four quarters.
value.literal: He also argued that when the Yellow Turbans were crushed in former times, agricultural colonies had been founded and grain piled at Xu so as to control the four quarters.

value.zh: 今三隅已定，事在淮南。
value.en: With three fronts quiet, only Huainan still mattered.
value.literal: Now the three corners were settled; what remained lay in Huainan.

value.zh: 每大軍征舉，運兵過半，功費巨億，以為大役。
value.en: Each campaign burned logistics—half the effort was convoys—and bills ran into billions of cash.
value.literal: Whenever great armies mobilized, more than half the burden was moving troops—costs ran to hundreds of millions and constituted a vast undertaking.

value.zh: 陳蔡之間，土下田良，可省許昌左右諸稻田，並水東下。
value.en: The Chen–Cai depression could soak up irrigation shed from the Xuchang rice plots if sluices turned east.
value.literal: Between Chen and Cai the ground was low and fertile; one could retire the paddy fields around Xuchang and send all the water eastward.

value.zh: 令淮北二萬人、淮南三萬人分休，且佃且守。
value.en: He proposed fifty thousand men alternating guard duty with tillage on both banks of the Huai.
value.literal: Order twenty thousand men north of the Huai and thirty thousand south of it to rotate rest with farming and guarding.

value.zh: 水豐，常收三倍于西，計除眾費，歲完五百萬斛以為軍資。
value.en: Wet years tripled western yields; after costs, five million hu a year could arm the campaigns.
value.literal: With abundant water, harvests constantly tripled those west of the river; deducting all expenses, five million hu could be delivered yearly for military supply.

value.zh: 六七年間，可積三千萬餘斛於淮北，此則十萬之眾五年食也。
value.en: Six or seven harvests could stack thirty million hu north of the river—five years' rations for a hundred-thousand-man host.
value.literal: In six or seven years one could stockpile over thirty million hu north of the Huai—food enough for an army of one hundred thousand for five years.

value.zh: 以此乘敵，無不克矣。
value.en: With this to strike the enemy, nothing would fail to be overcome.
value.literal: With this to strike the enemy, nothing would withstand you.

value.zh: 宣帝善之，皆如艾計施行。
value.en: Sima Yi signed off and executed Deng Ai's blueprint.
value.literal: Emperor Xuan approved it and implemented everything according to Ai's plan.

value.zh: 遂北臨淮水，自鐘離而南橫石以西，盡沘水四百餘里，五里置一營，營六十人，且佃且守。
value.en: They lined the Huai from Zhongli past Hengshi—four hundred li of Bi River front—posting sixty-man camps every five li to plough under arms.
value.literal: They therefore pressed north to the Huai River; from Zhongli south to west of Hengshi, and along the Bi River for over four hundred li, every five li they placed a camp of sixty men who farmed while they guarded.

value.zh: 兼修廣淮陽、百尺二渠，上引河流，下通淮潁，大治諸陂于潁南、潁北，穿渠三百餘里，溉田二萬頃，淮南、淮北皆相連接。
value.en: They dredged Huaiyang and Baichi, tied the Yellow River spill to Huai and Ying, refaced north–south Ying dikes, bored three hundred li of trench, and knitted Huai south and north across twenty thousand qing.
value.literal: They also widened the Huaiyang and Baichi canals, drawing the great river above and linking Huai and Ying below, greatly repairing the various weirs south and north of the Ying, cutting channels over three hundred li and irrigating twenty thousand qing of fields; Huainan and north of the Huai linked into one network.

value.zh: 自壽春到京師，農官兵田，雞犬之聲，阡陌相屬。
value.en: Between Shouchun and Luoyang, garrison farms crowded the roads—chickens and dogs crowding the same dikes.
value.literal: From Shouchun to the capital, military colonies lined the fields; the crowing of chickens and barking of dogs rose along paths that stretched unbroken.

value.zh: 每東南有事，大軍出征，泛舟而下，達于江淮，資食有儲，而無水害，艾所建也。
value.en: Whenever southeast campaigns launched, barges slid down safe channels to the Yangzi–Huai junction with grain to spare—Deng Ai's hydraulic shield.
value.literal: Whenever trouble arose in the southeast and great armies marched out, boats floated downstream to reach the Yangzi and Huai; provisions lay stored and flood harm was avoided—this was what Ai built.

value.zh: 言之不從，是謂不乂
value.en: When commands find no compliance, the canon calls it a failure of proper order.
value.literal: When commands find no compliance, the canon calls it a failure of proper order.

value.zh: 魏明帝太和二年五月，大旱。
value.en: Wei's Ming-di recorded a crushing drought in Taihe 2's fifth month.
value.literal: In the fifth month of Wei Emperor Ming's second Taihe year there was great drought.

value.zh: 元年以来崇廣宮府之應也。
value.en: Readers linked it to the endless new halls raised since Taihe began.
value.literal: This answered the expansion of palaces and offices since the first year of the era.

value.zh: 又，是春宣帝南擒孟達，置二郡，張郃西破諸葛亮，斃馬謖。
value.en: The same season saw Sima Yi seize Meng Da, Zhang He rout Zhuge Liang, and Ma Su die for his defeat.
value.literal: Moreover, that spring Emperor Xuan captured Meng Da in the south and set up two commanderies; Zhang He broke Zhuge Liang in the west and killed Ma Su.

value.zh: 亢陽自大，又其應也。
value.en: Another gloss: unchecked yang pride in the camp mirrored the weather.
value.literal: Yang arrogantly supreme — again its omen.

value.zh: 齊王正始元年二月，自去冬十二月至此月不雨。
value.en: Cao Fang's Zhengshi opening saw another rainless span from deep winter into early spring.
value.literal: In the second month of the Qi King's first Zhengshi year, from the twelfth month of last winter until this month it had not rained.

value.zh: 去歲正月，明帝崩。
value.en: Ming-di had fallen the previous new year.
value.literal: The first month of last year Emperor Ming died.

value.zh: 二月，曹爽白嗣主，轉宣帝為太傅，外示尊崇，內實欲令事先由已。
value.en: Cao Shuang "promoted" Sima Yi to figurehead tutor while hoarding real power.
value.literal: In the second month Cao Shuang informed the young lord, transferring Emperor Xuan to grand tutor, outwardly honoring him while in truth wishing every decision to pass through himself.

value.zh: 是時宣帝功蓋魏朝，欲德不用之應也。
value.en: Sima Yi's stature eclipsed the court — classic "latent virtue" portents.
value.literal: At that time Emperor Xuan's achievements overshadowed the Wei court — an omen of desired virtue unused.

value.zh: 景初初，童謠曰：「阿公阿公駕馬車，不意阿公東渡河，阿公來還當柰何！」
value.en: Early Jingchu, a children's rhyme said: "Grandpa, grandpa, drives a horse cart; never thought grandpa would ford the river east; grandpa comes back — what then!"
value.literal: Early Jingchu, a children's rhyme said: "Grandpa, grandpa, drives a horse cart; never thought grandpa would ford the river east; grandpa comes back — what then!"

value.zh: 及宣帝遼東歸，至白屋，當還鎮長安。
value.en: He should have turned west to Chang'an after the Liaodong campaign.
value.literal: When Emperor Xuan returned from Liaodong to Baiwu, he was to go back and garrison Chang'an.

value.zh: 會帝疾篤，急召之，乃乘追鋒車東渡河，終如童謠之言。
value.en: A dying summons sent him racing east instead, matching the omen.
value.literal: The emperor grew desperately ill and summoned him; he rode the "pursuit-blade" carriage east across the river — exactly as the rhyme said.

value.zh: 魏明帝青龍三年正月乙亥，隕石于壽光。
value.en: On yihai in the first month of Qinglong 3 under Wei Emperor Ming, a meteorite fell at Shouguang.
value.literal: Wei Emperor Ming, Qinglong 3, first month, yihai — a meteorite fell at Shouguang.

value.zh: 案《左氏傳》「隕石，星也」，劉歆說曰：「庶眾惟星隕于宋者，象宋襄公將得諸侯而不終也。」
value.en: The Zuo Tradition says "falling stone is a star"; Liu Xin explained: "When many stars fell on Song it signified Duke Xiang gaining the hegemons yet not finishing."
value.literal: The Zuo Tradition says "falling stone is a star"; Liu Xin explained: "When many stars fell on Song it signified Duke Xiang gaining the hegemons yet not finishing."

value.zh: 秦始皇時有隕石，班固以為：「石，陰類也。
value.en: Qin Shihuang had meteorites; Ban Gu thought: "Stone is yin class.
value.literal: Qin Shihuang had meteorites; Ban Gu thought: "Stone is yin class.

value.zh: 又白祥，臣將危君。」
value.en: Also white omen — ministers will endanger the ruler."
value.literal: Also white omen — ministers will endanger the ruler."

value.zh: 是後宣帝得政云。
value.en: Sima Yi followed the omen.
value.literal: Thereafter Emperor Xuan seized power.

value.zh: 夫乾坤定位，男女流形，伉儷之義同歸，貴賤之名異等。
value.en: Heaven and earth fixed their stations; men and women took their bodily shapes. Husband and wife share one moral purpose, even though rank divides high from low.
value.literal: As for Qian and Kun taking their positions, male and female receive their forms; the principle of husband and wife aims at the same end, yet the names of noble and base stand in different ranks.

value.zh: 若乃作配皇極，齊體紫宸，象玉床之連後星，喻金波之合羲璧。
value.en: Those who match the sovereign on high and share the body politic of the inner palace are figured as the jade couch tied to the queen’s asterism, as moonlight married to the solar disk.
value.literal: When one is paired with the supreme apex and shares the substance of the Purple Palace, it is likened to the jade couch linking to the rear stars, and compared to golden waves joining the Xi disk.

value.zh: 爰自敻古，是謂元妃；
value.en: In deepest antiquity she was known as the principal wife;
value.literal: From remote antiquity onward, she was called the chief consort;

value.zh: 降及中年，乃稱王后。
value.en: Later ages styled her queen.
value.literal: Descending to middle antiquity, she was then titled queen.

value.zh: 四人並列，光于帝嚳之宮；
value.en: Four consorts stood side by side and brought glory to Emperor Ku’s inner court;
value.literal: Four women stood ranked together, shining in the palace of Emperor Ku;

value.zh: 二妃同降，著彼有虞之典。
value.en: Two royal brides arrived together and entered the canonical record of Shun’s reign.
value.literal: Two consorts descended together, written into the canons of Yu’s age.

value.zh: 夏商以上，六宮之制，其詳靡得而聞焉。
value.en: For ages before Xia and Shang, no reliable detail survives about how the six wings of the harem were ordered.
value.literal: Above Xia and Shang, the regulations of the Six Palaces cannot be heard of in detail.

value.zh: 姬劉以降，五翟之規，其事可略而言矣。
value.en: From the Zhou and Han dynasties on, the graded “five pheasant” ritual for consorts can at least be sketched.
value.literal: From Ji and Liu onward, the rules of the five pheasant insignia may be spoken of in outline.

value.zh: 周禮，天子立一后、三夫人、九嬪、二十七世婦、八十一御妻，以聽王者內政。
value.en: The Rites of Zhou prescribe one empress, three chief consorts, nine ranked ladies, twenty-seven secondary wives, and eighty-one attendants to manage the sovereign’s domestic government.
value.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the Son of Heaven establishes one queen, three ladies, nine bin, twenty-seven wives of rank, and eighty-one minor wives, to administer the king’s inner administration.

value.zh: 故婚義曰：「天子之與后，如日之與月，陰之與陽。」
value.en: The Meaning of Marriage therefore declares: “The emperor and his empress mirror sun and moon, yin and yang.”
value.literal: Therefore the Meaning of Marriage says: “The Son of Heaven and the queen are like sun and moon, yin and yang.”

value.zh: 由斯而談，其所從來遠矣。
value.en: Judged by such language, their institution reaches far back into antiquity.
value.literal: From this perspective, what they derive from is distant indeed.

value.zh: 故能母儀天宇，助宣王化，德均載物，比大坤維，宗廟歆其薦羞，穹壤俟其交泰。
value.en: Hence she sets the maternal standard for the realm, advances the king’s civilizing work, and bears creation as steadfastly as earth itself; the temple accepts her sacrifices gladly, and heaven and earth look to her union with the throne for peace.
value.literal: Thus she can be the motherly model for all under heaven, aid in spreading royal transformation, her virtue evenly bearing all things, comparable to the great sustaining power of Kun; the ancestral temple delights in her offerings, heaven and earth await her harmonizing union.

value.zh: 是以哲王垂憲，尤重造舟之禮；
value.en: That is why enlightened monarchs codify law and prize above all the royal wedding rite of “meeting across the boat.”
value.literal: Therefore wise kings hang forth statutes and especially esteem the rite of the built bridge;

value.zh: 詩人立言，先獎葛覃之訓。
value.en: The Classic of Poetry opens by honoring the lessons of “Ge Tan,” the ode on diligent royal ladies.
value.literal: The poets set forth words and first praise the instruction of “Ge Tan.”

value.zh: 後燭流景，所以裁其宴私；
value.en: Dimming the late-night lamp curbs excess in the privy chamber;
value.literal: The rear candle’s flowing light is the means to regulate their private banquets;

value.zh: 房樂希聲，是用節其容止。
value.en: Sparse music in the inner rooms reins in conduct at court and couch alike.
value.literal: Chamber music with sparse sound is the means to moderate their bearing.

value.zh: 履端正本，抑斯之謂歟！
value.en: Walking straight to set the root right—surely this is what those measures intend!
value.literal: Walking upright to rectify the root—is this not what is meant!

value.zh: 若乃娉納有方，防閑有禮，肅尊儀而修四德，體柔範而弘六義，陰教洽于宮闈，淑譽騰於區域。
value.en: When matches are arranged by rule, propriety fences passion, majesty guards ritual while the four womanly virtues are cultivated, gentle models enlarge the six canonical lessons, inner-chamber teaching fills the harem, and fair fame spreads beyond the capital.
value.literal: If betrothal and intake have proper method, fences and restraint have ritual, reverently honoring ceremony while cultivating the four virtues, embodying gentle norms while extending the six meanings, then women’s instruction permeates the palace, and good reputation rises through the regions.

value.zh: 則玄雲入戶，上帝錫母萌之符；
value.en: Then auspicious clouds cross the threshold and Heaven grants the token of fruitful motherhood;
value.literal: Then dark clouds enter the door, and the Supreme Lord grants the sign of motherhood’s sprouting;

value.zh: 黃神降徵，坤靈贊壽丘之道，終能鼎祚惟永，胤嗣克昌。
value.en: The divine Yellow Emperor sends portents; earth’s spirit blesses the birth-hill of sage-kings; the dynasty’s mandate endures and heirs thrive.
value.literal: The Yellow Spirit sends down omens; the spirit of Kun assists the way of Shouqiu; ultimately the tripod fortune can be everlasting and heirs flourish.

value.zh: 至若儷極虧閑，憑天作孽，倒裳衣于衽席，感朓側於弦望。
value.en: But women who reach the throne yet abandon modesty, who invoke Heaven while plotting harm, who turn proper dress upside down on the bed, and whose passions shift with every phase of the moon—
value.literal: As for those paired to the apex yet deficient in restraint, who rely on heaven to work calamity, who overturn upper and lower garments upon the mat, and feel lust askew at first quarter and full moon.

value.zh: 則龍漦結釁，宗周鞠為黍苗；
value.en: —dragon spit seals a fatal feud, and the Zhou heartland turns to weed-grown ruin;
value.literal: Then dragon-spittle knots disaster, and royal Zhou becomes nothing but millet shoots;

value.zh: 燕尾挻災，隆漢墜其枌社矣。
value.en: swallow-tail charms invite catastrophe, and even mighty Han loses its soil-and-millet shrines.
value.literal: Swallow tails draw calamity, and flourishing Han drops its mulberry altars.

value.zh: 自曹劉內主，位以色登，甄衛之家，榮非德舉。
value.en: Under the Cao and Liu courts, palace ladies rose by looks alone; clans such as the Zhens and Weis won favor without moral merit.
value.literal: Since the inner mistresses of Cao and Liu, position climbed by beauty; in the households of Zhen and Wei, glory was not raised by virtue.

value.zh: 淫荒挺性，蔑西郊之禮容；
value.en: Wanton temperaments mocked the solemn suburban liturgy reserved for the empress;
value.literal: Dissolute and wasteful by nature, they slighted the ritual bearing of the western suburb;

value.zh: 婉孌含辭，作南國之奇態。
value.en: Soft voices and studied phrases invented the freakish grace of southern entertainers.
value.literal: Soft loveliness holding coy phrases, they fashioned exotic manners of the southern states.

value.zh: 詖謁由斯外人，穢德於是內宣。
value.en: Sycophancy leaked beyond the palace gates while depravity was preached inside.
value.literal: Slanderous flattery thereby passed outward, and foul conduct was proclaimed within.

value.zh: 椒掖播晨牝之風，蘭殿絕河雎之響。
value.en: The harem aired the omen of women ruling like crowing hens; orchid halls no longer echoed the chaste songs of “Guan ju.”
value.literal: The pepper chambers spread the wind of the hen crowing at dawn; the orchid halls cut off the echo of “Guan ju” by the River.

value.zh: 永言彤史，大練之範逾微；
value.en: Forever the palace diarists wrote, yet the ideal of homespun austerity faded;
value.literal: Speaking long of the vermilion scribe, the model of coarse white silk grows ever fainter;

value.zh: 緬視青蒲，脫珥之猷替矣。
value.en: Looking back to mat audiences where consorts remonstrated, the counsel of tearing off earrings to warn the throne had vanished.
value.literal: Gazing afar at the green rushes, the strategy of casting off ear-jewels is replaced.

value.zh: 晉承其末，與世污隆，宣皇創基，功弘而道屈；
value.en: The Jin took up this fallen era and rose or fell with the times. Emperor Xuan laid the foundations: his deeds were grand, yet the moral course stayed cramped;
value.literal: Jin inherited the late age; with the world it sank and rose. Emperor Xuan founded the base—achievement broad yet the Way bent;

value.zh: 穆后一善，勣侔於十亂。
value.en: a single virtue in Empress Mu rivaled the merit of the “ten turbulent” worthies who saved a dynasty.
value.literal: one goodness of Empress Mu—merit equal to the Ten Disorderly Ones.

value.zh: 洎乎世祖，[1]始親選良家，既而帝掩紈扇，躬行請託。
value.en: Under Emperor Wu [1] the court at first picked brides from respectable houses; soon the sovereign waved his silk fan in the inner quarters and himself traded favors for appointments.
value.literal: Down to Shizu [1], he began personally selecting from good families; thereafter the emperor hid behind the silk fan and personally practiced solicitation.

value.zh: 后採長白，實彰妒忌之情；
value.en: An empress chosen for graying hair laid bare the spite of jealousy;
value.literal: The empress chose “long white,” truly displaying jealousy;

value.zh: 賈納短青，竟踐覆亡之轍。
value.en: the Jias welcomed a young rival and eventually followed the same rut to ruin.
value.literal: Jia took in “short green,” and in the end trod the rut of overthrow.

value.zh: 得失遺跡，煥在綈緗，興滅所由，義同畫一。
value.en: Success and failure still gleam from the silk-bound histories; the springs of fortune and disaster follow one clear pattern.
value.literal: Tracks of gain and loss shine forth on silk documents; the causes of rise and ruin share one uniform pattern in meaning.

value.zh: 故列其本事，以為后妃傳云。
value.en: I therefore set out the essential facts as this “Treatise on Empresses and Consorts.”
value.literal: Therefore I array their basic affairs to form this treatise on empresses and consorts.

value.zh: 宣穆張皇后諱春華，河內平皋人也。
value.en: Empress Zhang Xuanmu, personal name Chunhua, came from Pinggao in Henei commandery.
value.literal: Empress Zhang Xuanmu, taboo name Chunhua, was a native of Pinggao in Henei.

value.zh: 父汪，魏粟邑令；
value.en: Her father Wang had served as magistrate of Suiyi under Wei;
value.literal: Her father Wang was magistrate of Suiyi in Wei;

value.zh: 母河內山氏，司徒濤之從祖姑也。
value.en: her mother was a Shan from Henei, first cousin once removed to Grand Tutor Shan Tao.
value.literal: her mother was a Shan of Henei, a paternal grand-aunt by cousinship of Minister of Education Tao.

value.zh: 后少有德行，智識過人，生景帝、文帝、平原王幹、南陽公主。
value.en: She showed virtue and unusual discernment from girlhood. She was mother to Emperors Jing and Wen, to Prince Sima Gan of Pingyuan, and to the Princess of Nanyang.
value.literal: The empress from youth had virtuous conduct and intelligence surpassing others; she bore Emperor Jing, Emperor Wen, Prince Gan of Pingyuan, and the Princess of Nanyang.

value.zh: 宣帝初辭魏武之命，託以風痹，嘗暴書，遇暴雨，不覺自起收之。
value.en: When Emperor Xuan first refused Cao Cao’s summons, claiming crippling palsy, he once aired books in the sun. A cloudburst came; forgetting his act, he leapt up to rescue them.
value.literal: When Emperor Xuan at first declined Wei Wu’s summons, pleading wind paralysis, he once sunned books; encountering a sudden storm, unthinkingly he rose himself to gather them in.

value.zh: 家惟有一婢見之，后乃恐事泄致禍，遂手殺之以滅口，而親自執爨。
value.en: A single bondmaid witnessed it. Fearing exposure would destroy them, the empress killed her with her own hands and herself cooked the family meals to hide the truth.
value.literal: Only one maid in the house saw it; the empress then feared the affair leaking and bringing disaster, so she personally killed her to silence her, and herself attended the cooking stove.

value.zh: 帝由是重之。
value.en: Thereafter her husband valued her all the more.
value.literal: The emperor from this esteemed her.

value.zh: 其後柏夫人有寵，后罕得進見。
value.en: Later Lady Bai won his favor, and the empress was seldom admitted.
value.literal: Afterward Lady Bai had favor, and the empress rarely obtained audience.

value.zh: 帝嘗臥疾，后往省病。
value.en: Once when he lay sick, she came to nurse him.
value.literal: The emperor once lay ill; the empress went to inquire after his illness.

value.zh: 帝曰：「老物可憎，何煩出也！」
value.en: He snapped, “That foul old hag—why drag herself here!”
value.literal: The emperor said: “That old creature is hateful—why trouble to come out!”

value.zh: 后慚恚不食，將自殺，諸子亦不食。
value.en: Shamed and furious, she refused food and meant to take her life; her sons fasted with her.
value.literal: The empress, ashamed and enraged, did not eat and was about to kill herself; her sons likewise did not eat.

value.zh: 帝驚而致謝，后乃止。
value.en: Alarmed, he apologized, and she gave up the attempt.
value.literal: The emperor was alarmed and apologized; the empress then stopped.

value.zh: 帝退而謂人曰：「老物不足惜，慮困我好兒耳！」
value.en: Privately he muttered, “I care nothing for the hag—I fear only harm to my fine sons.”
value.literal: The emperor withdrew and said to someone: “The old creature is not worth pity—I worry she will distress my good sons!”

value.zh: 后雅有識度，帝每有所為，必豫籌畫。
value.en: She was poised and far-sighted; whatever her husband planned, she anticipated and shaped.
value.literal: The empress elegantly had insight and measure; whenever the emperor had something to do, she always planned ahead.

value.zh: 魏明帝世，宣帝居上將之重，諸子並有雄才大略。
value.en: Under Wei Mingdi, Sima Yi commanded the armies while his sons showed ruthless ambition.
value.literal: In Emperor Ming of Wei’s reign, Emperor Xuan occupied the weight of supreme commander; his sons all had heroic talent and broad strategies.

value.zh: 后知帝非魏之純臣，而后既魏氏之甥，帝深忌之。
value.en: She knew Sima Yi was no loyal servant of Wei, yet as a Wei princess by birth she herself drew his deepest suspicion.
value.literal: The empress knew the emperor was not a pure minister of Wei, yet the empress was moreover a niece of the Wei clan—deeply the emperor suspected her.

value.zh: 青龍二年，遂以鴆崩，時年二十四，葬峻平陵。
value.en: In 234 she was poisoned at twenty-four and buried at Junping mausoleum.
value.literal: In the second Qinglong year she then died by poisoned wine, aged twenty-four, buried at Junping tumulus.

value.zh: 武帝登阼，初未追崇，弘訓太后每以為言，泰始二年始加號諡。
value.en: After Emperor Wu took the throne he left her unhonored until Empress Dowager Yang at Hongxun repeatedly pressed the matter; only in 266 did he grant posthumous rank and epithet.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, at first he did not posthumously honor her; Empress Dowager Hongxun often spoke of it; only in the second Taishi year did he begin adding title and posthumous name.

value.zh: 后無男，生五女。
value.en: She had no sons but five daughters.
value.literal: The empress had no sons; she bore five daughters.

value.zh: 安平獻王孚
value.en: Prince Xian of Anping, Sima Fu.
value.literal: Prince Fu of Anping with posthumous title Xian (section heading).

value.zh: 安平獻王孚，字叔達，宣帝次弟也。
value.en: Sima Fu, Prince Xian of Anping, styled Shuda, was the younger brother who followed Emperor Xuan (Sima Yi).
value.literal: Prince Xian of Anping, Sima Fu, courtesy name Shuda, was Emperor Xuan's next younger brother.

value.zh: 初，孚長兄朗字伯達，宣帝字仲達，孚弟馗字季達，恂字顯達，進字惠達，通字雅達，敏字幼達，俱知名，故時號為「八達」焉。
value.en: At first Fu's eldest brother Lang had courtesy name Boda; Emperor Xuan had courtesy name Zhongda; Fu's younger brothers were Kui, courtesy Jida; Xun, Xianda; Jin, Huida; Tong, Yada; and Min, Youda; all were renowned, so people at the time called them the 'Eight Worthies.'
value.literal: At first Fu's eldest brother Lang had courtesy name Boda; Emperor Xuan had courtesy name Zhongda; Fu's younger brothers were Kui, courtesy Jida; Xun, Xianda; Jin, Huida; Tong, Yada; and Min, Youda; all were renowned, so people at the time called them the 'Eight Worthies.'

value.zh: 孚溫厚廉讓，博涉經史。
value.en: Warm, modest, and widely read in classical texts and history, he carried himself with unassuming grace.
value.literal: Fu was warm and generous, honest and yielding, and broadly read the Classics and histories.

value.zh: 漢末喪亂，與兄弟處危亡之中，簞食瓢飲，而披閱不倦。
value.en: Through the Han collapse he and his brothers lived on the verge of ruin on the plainest fare, yet he never tired of his books.
value.literal: At the end of the Han there was turmoil and disorder; with his brothers he dwelt amid peril and extinction, eating from bamboo baskets and drinking from gourd dippers, yet he wearied not of reading.

value.zh: 性通恕，以貞白自立，未嘗有怨於人。
value.en: Forgiving by temperament and upright in reputation, he kept himself blameless and bore no grudges.
value.literal: By nature he was open and forgiving; by purity and integrity he established himself, and he never harbored resentment toward anyone.

value.zh: 陳留殷武有名於海內，嘗罹罪譴，孚往省之，遂與同處分食，談者稱焉。
value.en: When Yin Wu of Chenliu—a man celebrated empire-wide—was censured and punished, Fu called on him and stayed to share quarters and meals; observers admired his loyalty.
value.literal: Yin Wu of Chenliu had renown throughout the realm; he once suffered condemnation for an offense. Fu went to visit him and shared lodging and divided food with him; those who spoke of it praised him.

value.zh: 時孫權稱籓，請送任子，當遣前將軍于禁還，久而不至。
value.en: Sun Quan had submitted as a tributary and offered to send a royal hostage and return the captive Yu Jin—but neither pledge appeared.
value.literal: At that time Sun Quan declared himself a vassal and requested to send a hostage son; it was intended to send back former general Yu Jin, but after a long time he still had not arrived.

value.zh: 天子以問孚，孚曰：「先王設九服之制，誠以要荒難以德懷，不以諸夏禮責也。
value.en: The Son of Heaven asked Fu about it. Fu said, 'The former kings established the nine domains system—truly because the distant and wild regions are hard to win by virtue alone, and they did not hold them to Central States ritual.
value.literal: The Son of Heaven asked Fu about it. Fu said, 'The former kings established the nine domains system—truly because the distant and wild regions are hard to win by virtue alone, and they did not hold them to Central States ritual.

value.zh: 陛下承緒，遠人率貢。
value.en: Your Majesty carries on the succession; distant peoples all come bearing tribute.
value.literal: Your Majesty carries on the succession; distant peoples all come bearing tribute.

value.zh: 權雖未送任子，於禁不至，猶宜以寬待之，畜養士馬，以觀其變。
value.en: Though Quan has not yet sent the hostage son and Yu Jin has not arrived, still it is fitting to treat him generously, nurture soldiers and horses, and observe how matters change.
value.literal: Though Quan has not yet sent the hostage son and Yu Jin has not arrived, still it is fitting to treat him generously, nurture soldiers and horses, and observe how matters change.

value.zh: 不可以嫌疑責讓，恐傷懷遠之義。
value.en: One must not on account of suspicion reproach and blame him, lest one wound the principle of cherishing those far away.
value.literal: One must not on account of suspicion reproach and blame him, lest one wound the principle of cherishing those far away.

value.zh: 自孫策至權，奕世相繼，惟強與弱，不在一禁，禁之未至，當有他故耳。」
value.en: From Sun Ce down to Quan, generations succeed one another; strength and weakness lie not in one Yu Jin; when Jin does not arrive, there ought to be another reason.'
value.literal: From Sun Ce down to Quan, generations succeed one another; strength and weakness lie not in one Yu Jin; when Jin does not arrive, there ought to be another reason.'

value.zh: 後禁至，果以疾遲留，而任子竟不至。
value.en: Yu Jin eventually appeared, detained by illness as Fu predicted, yet the hostage never followed.
value.literal: Afterward Jin arrived; indeed he had delayed because of illness, yet in the end the hostage son never came.

value.zh: 大軍臨江，責其違言，吳遂絕不貢獻。
value.en: Once imperial troops stood on the river and challenged Wu's breach of faith, tribute from the south stopped altogether.
value.literal: When the great army reached the Yangzi they blamed Wu for breaking its word, and Wu then utterly ceased tribute.

value.zh: 後出為河內典農，賜爵關內侯，轉清河太守。
value.en: He later served as Henei agrarian director, received a secondary marquisate within the passes, then governed Qinghe.
value.literal: Later he went out as Agrarian Director for Henei, was enfeoffed with rank of district marquis within the passes, and transferred to governor of Qinghe.

value.zh: 初，魏文帝置度支尚書，專掌軍國支計，朝議以征討未息，動須節量。
value.en: Emperor Wen had created the revenue ministry for military supply; court opinion stressed ongoing campaigns meant every outlay needed restraint.
value.literal: At first Wei Emperor Wen established the Minister of Revenue to specialize in army and state expenditures; court discussion held that with expeditions still unfinished, movements constantly required moderation.

value.zh: 及明帝嗣位，欲用孚，問左右曰：「有兄風不？」
value.en: When Emperor Ming succeeded to the throne and wished to employ Fu, he asked those around him, "Does he have his elder brother's manner?"
value.literal: When Emperor Ming succeeded to the throne and wished to employ Fu, he asked those around him, "Does he have his elder brother's manner?"

value.zh: 答云：「似兄。」
value.en: They answered, "He resembles his elder brother."
value.literal: They answered, "He resembles his elder brother."

value.zh: 天子曰：「吾得司馬懿二人，復何憂哉！」
value.en: The Son of Heaven said, 'If I obtain two Sima Yis, what else need I worry about!'
value.literal: The Son of Heaven said, 'If I obtain two Sima Yis, what else need I worry about!'

value.zh: 轉為度支尚書。
value.en: He was named minister of revenue.
value.literal: Fu was transferred to Minister of Revenue.

value.zh: 孚以為擒敵制勝，宜有備預。
value.en: Fu insisted victory required planning ahead.
value.literal: Fu held that to seize the enemy and achieve victory there ought to be preparedness beforehand.

value.zh: 每諸葛亮入寇關中，邊兵不能制敵，中軍奔赴，輒不及事機，宜預選步騎二萬，以為二部，為討賊之備。
value.en: Each time Zhuge Liang struck Guanzhong the border garrisons buckled while reinforcements arrived too late; Fu urged standing two corps of twenty thousand foot and horse in readiness.
value.literal: Whenever Zhuge Liang invaded Guanzhong, the frontier troops could not check the enemy and the central army rushed to the rescue but always missed the moment; he proposed beforehand to select twenty thousand infantry and cavalry and divide them into two corps as preparations for punishing the rebels.

value.zh: 又以關中連遭賊寇，穀帛不足，遣冀州農丁五千屯於上邽，秋冬習戰陣，春夏修田桑。
value.en: With Guanzhong stripped by raids and short of grain and cloth, he relocated five thousand Ji cultivators to Shanggui to drill in winter and farm in summer.
value.literal: Also because Guanzhong had repeatedly suffered bandit raids and grain and silk were insufficient, he sent five thousand farming households from Ji Province to garrison Shanggui; in autumn and winter they drilled battle formations, in spring and summer they tended fields and mulberries.

value.zh: 由是關中軍國有餘，待賊有備矣。
value.en: The western theater grew solvent while keeping the foe under watch.
value.literal: By this means Guanzhong's army and state had surplus and awaited the enemy prepared.

value.zh: 後除尚書右僕射，進爵昌平亭侯，遷尚書令。
value.en: He rose to right vice director of the secretariat, marquis of Changping ting, then director.
value.literal: Later he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, advanced in rank to Marquis of Changping precinct, and promoted Director of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 及大將軍曹爽擅權，李勝、何晏、鄧颺等亂政，孚不視庶事，但正身遠害而已。
value.en: Under Cao Shuang's dictatorship and the cabal of Li Sheng, He Yan, and Deng Yang, Fu withdrew from daily administration and merely kept his head down.
value.literal: When Grand General Cao Shuang monopolized power and Li Sheng, He Yan, Deng Yang, and others threw government into chaos, Fu did not attend to routine affairs but simply corrected himself and kept distant from harm.

value.zh: 及宣帝誅爽，孚與景帝屯司馬門，以功進爵長社縣侯，加侍中。
value.en: When Sima Yi struck down Shuang, Fu and Sima Shi sealed Sima Gate; for that service he became marquis of Changshe and palace attendant.
value.literal: When Emperor Xuan executed Shuang, Fu together with Emperor Jing held Sima Gate; by merit he advanced to marquis of Changshe county and was additionally appointed palace attendant.

value.zh: 及高貴鄉公遭害，百官莫敢奔赴，孚枕屍於股，哭之慟，曰：「殺陛下者臣之罪。」
value.en: When the Duke of Gaoguixiang suffered violent death, none of the hundred officials dared go to the scene; Fu pillowed the corpse on his thigh, wept bitterly, and said, 'Those who killed Your Majesty are my crime.'
value.literal: When the Duke of Gaoguixiang suffered violent death, none of the hundred officials dared go to the scene; Fu pillowed the corpse on his thigh, wept bitterly, and said, 'Those who killed Your Majesty are my crime.'

value.zh: 奏推主者。
value.en: He filed charges against the ringleaders.
value.literal: He memorialized to pursue those responsible.

value.zh: 會太后令以庶人禮葬，孚與群公上表，乞以王禮葬，從之。
value.en: Though the empress dowager first demanded a commoner's funeral, Fu and his peers petitioned for kingly honors and won consent.
value.literal: When it happened that the empress dowager ordered burial by commoner rites, Fu together with the dukes submitted a memorial begging burial by princely rites; she assented.

value.zh: 孚性至慎。
value.en: By temperament he was exceedingly careful.
value.literal: Fu's nature was extremely cautious.

value.zh: 宣帝執政，常自退損。
value.en: Under Sima Yi's supremacy he habitually effaced himself.
value.literal: When Emperor Xuan held power he often withdrew and diminished himself.

value.zh: 後逢廢立之際，未嘗預謀。
value.en: At every coup and enthronement thereafter he kept clear of the plotting.
value.literal: Later when occasions of deposition and enthronement came, he never participated in plotting.

value.zh: 景文二帝以孚屬尊，不敢逼。
value.en: Sima Shi and Sima Zhao honored his seniority and never leaned on him.
value.literal: Emperors Jing and Wen, because Fu's standing was venerable, did not dare coerce him.

value.zh: 後進封長樂公。
value.en: He was later advanced to duke of Changle.
value.literal: Later he was advanced and enfeoffed as duke of Changle.

value.zh: =義陽成王望，字子初，出繼伯父朗，寬厚有父風。
value.en: Sima Wang, Prince Cheng of Yiyang, styled Zichu, was adopted into uncle Sima Lang's line—open-handed and steady like his father.
value.literal: Prince Cheng of Yiyang, Wang, courtesy Zichu, went out to succeed uncle Lang; he was generous and mild and had his father's manner.

value.zh: 仕郡上計吏，舉孝廉，辟司徒掾，曆平陽太守、洛陽典農中郎將。
value.en: He rose from commandery accountant through filial-incorrupt recommendation and ministerial aide to Pingyang governor and Luoyang agrarian colonel.
value.literal: He served the commandery as accounts clerk, was recommended Filial and Incorrupt, was summoned as aide to the Minister of Education, and successively held governor of Pingyang and Agrarian Commandant of Luoyang.

value.zh: 從宣帝討王淩，以功封永安亭侯。
value.en: Campaigning with Sima Yi against Wang Ling earned him the Yong'an ting marquisate.
value.literal: He followed Emperor Xuan to punish Wang Ling and by merit was enfeoffed Marquis of Yong'an precinct.

value.zh: 遷護軍將軍，改封安樂鄉侯，加散騎常侍。
value.en: Promoted general who guards the army, he exchanged his fief for Anle township and received supernumerary cavalry attendant rank.
value.literal: He was promoted General Who Guards the Army, changed enfeoffment to Marquis of Anle village, and added irregular cavalry attendant.

value.zh: 時魏高貴鄉公好才愛士，望與裴秀、王沈、鍾會並見親待，數侍宴筵。
value.en: Cao Mao cultivated writers and thinkers; Wang joined Pei Xiu, Wang Chen, and Zhong Hui in the emperor's intimate circle at countless banquets.
value.literal: At that time Wei Duke of Gaoguixiang loved talent and cherished scholars; Wang together with Pei Xiu, Wang Chen, and Zhong Hui alike saw intimate favor and repeatedly attended banquets.

value.zh: 公性急，秀等居內職，急有召便至。
value.en: The sovereign's temper ran hot; men like Pei Xiu, holding palace posts, could answer an urgent summons immediately.
value.literal: The duke was impatient by nature; Xiu and others held inner posts and when urgently summoned arrived at once.

value.zh: 以望外官，特給追鋒車一乘，武賁五人。
value.en: As an outsider he was granted a rapid courier cart and five household guards.
value.literal: Because Wang was an outer official, specially there was given one swift-response carriage and five palace runners.

value.zh: 時景文相繼輔政，未嘗朝覲，權歸晉室。
value.en: Sima Shi and Sima Zhao ruled behind the curtain without formal audiences—effective authority already rested with the future Jin house.
value.literal: At that time Jing and Wen succeeded each other as regents and never held court audience; power returned to the Jin house.

value.zh: 望雖見寵待，每不自安，由是求出，為征西將軍、持節、都督雍涼二州諸軍事。
value.en: Royal favor could not settle him; he won a western command as conquering-general with credentials over Yong and Liang.
value.literal: Though Wang saw favor and treatment, often he was not at ease; on this account he sought to go out and became General Who Conquers the West, bearer of credentials, and supervisor of all military affairs of Yong and Liang provinces.

value.zh: 在任八年，威化明肅。
value.en: Across eight years his governance ran lucid and austere.
value.literal: In office eight years, his awe-inspiring transformation was bright and stern.

value.zh: 先是蜀將薑維屢寇關中，及望至，廣設方略，維不得為寇，關中賴之。
value.en: After Jiang Wei's repeated strikes on Guanzhong, Wang's strategy stopped further incursions and steadied the northwest.
value.literal: Earlier Shu general Jiang Wei repeatedly raided Guanzhong; when Wang arrived he broadly laid plans and measures so Wei could not raid; Guanzhong relied on him.

value.zh: 進封順陽侯。
value.en: His fief rose to marquis of Shunyang.
value.literal: He was advanced and enfeoffed Marquis of Shunyang.

value.zh: 徵拜衛將軍，領中領軍，典禁兵。
value.en: Recalled as metropolitan guard, he headed the central army and commanded palace soldiers.
value.literal: He was summoned and appointed General Who Guards the Metropolis, concurrently Central Army Supervisor, in charge of palace troops.

value.zh: 尋加驃騎將軍、開府。
value.en: He soon added champion-general rank with an independent staff.
value.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed Champion General and granted independent headquarters.

value.zh: 頃之，代何曾為司徒。
value.en: Shortly afterward he succeeded He Zeng as minister of education.
value.literal: Before long he replaced He Zeng as Minister of Education.

value.zh: 彭城穆王權，字子輿，宣帝弟魏魯相東武城侯馗之子也。
value.en: Sima Quan, King Mu of Pengcheng and styled Ziyu, was the son of Sima Kui, Marquis of Dongwucheng and governor of Lu under Wei, who was Sima Yi's younger brother.
value.literal: Prince Mu of Pengcheng Quan courtesy Ziyu was son of Emperor Xuan's younger brother Wei Lu governor East Wucheng Marquis Kui.

value.zh: 初襲封，拜冗從僕射。
value.en: He opened as supernumerary chariot master.
value.literal: At first inheriting the enfeoffment he was appointed Supernumerary Master of Chariots.

value.zh: 武帝受禪，封彭城王，邑二千九百戶。
value.en: Sima Yan made him Pengcheng prince at 2,900 households.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Pengcheng with two thousand nine hundred households.

value.zh: 出為北中郎將、都督鄴城守諸軍事。
value.en: He commanded Ye's northern gentleman garrison.
value.literal: He went out as General of the Northern Gentlemen supervising Ye city garrison affairs.

value.zh: 泰始中入朝，賜袞冕之服。
value.en: Mid-Taishi brought court investiture robes.
value.literal: In Taishi mid-years he entered court and was granted robe and crown of state.

value.zh: 咸甯元年薨，子元王植立。
value.en: 275 death; Yuan prince Zhi followed.
value.literal: In Xianning year one he died; son Prince Yuan Zhi succeeded.

value.zh: 歷位後將軍，尋拜國子祭酒、太僕卿、侍中、尚書。
value.en: His offices ran rear general, academy libationer, coach minister, palace attendant, and ministry.
value.literal: He successively held Later General, soon appointed Libationer of the Imperial Academy, Minister of Coachmanship, palace attendant, and minister of writing.

value.zh: 出為安東將軍、都督揚州諸軍事，代淮南王允鎮壽春，未發。
value.en: Named east-pacifier for Yangzhou replacing Yun at Shouchun, he never took up post.
value.literal: He was going out as General Who Pacifies the East supervising Yangzhou military affairs replacing Prince Huainan Yun at Shouchun but did not depart.

value.zh: 或云植助允攻趙王倫，遂以憂薨。
value.en: Tradition claims he aided Yun against Sima Lun and died of anxiety.
value.literal: Some say Zhi assisted Yun in attacking Prince Zhao Lun and therefore died of grief.

value.zh: 贈車騎將軍，增封萬五千戶。
value.en: The court added posthumous chariot-and-cavalry honors and boosted his fief by fifteen thousand households.
value.literal: He was posthumously invested chariot-and-cavalry general and his enfeoffment was increased by fifteen thousand households.

value.zh: 子康王釋立，官至南中郎將、持節、平南將軍，分魯國蕃、薛二縣以益其國，心二萬三千戶。
value.en: Prince Kang Sima Shi rose to southern gentleman-general with pacifying-south command, annexed Fan and Xue from Lu, and held twenty-three thousand households.
value.literal: Son Prince Kang Shi succeeded; he reached Southern Gentlemen General, credential-bearing, Pacifying South General; partitioned Fan and Xue counties of Lu to enlarge his state; total twenty-three thousand households.

value.zh: 薨，子雄立，坐奔蘇峻伏誅，更以釋子紘嗣。
value.en: After his death Xiong inherited but died with Su Jun's rebellion; Hong, son of Shi, continued the line.
value.literal: He died; son Xiong succeeded; Xiong was executed for fleeing to Su Jun; Shi's son Hong was changed to succeed.

value.zh: 濟南惠王遂，字子伯，宣帝弟魏鴻臚丞恂之子也。
value.en: Sima Sui, styled Zibo, was Sima Xun's son—Sima Yi's nephew.
value.literal: Prince Hui of Jinan Sui courtesy Zibo was son of Emperor Xuan's younger brother Wei Grand Herald Assistant Xun.

value.zh: 仕魏關內侯，進封平昌亭侯，曆典軍郎將，
value.en: Under Wei he rose from secondary marquis to Pingchang ting through army posts.
value.literal: Serving Wei district marquis within passes advanced Marquis of Pingchang precinct successively holding army corps captain.

value.zh: 景元二年，轉封武城鄉侯、督鄴城守諸軍事、北中郎將。
value.en: In the second year of Jingyuan, Shifted to Wucheng township marquis guarding Ye as northern gentleman.
value.literal: In the second year of Jingyuan, Transferred enfeoffment Wucheng village marquis supervising Ye garrison Northern Gentlemen General.

value.zh: 五等建，封祝阿伯，累遷冠軍將軍。
value.en: Five-rank reform made him Zhu'e baron then champion general.
value.literal: When five ranks were established enfeoffed Baron of Zhu'e progressively Champion General.

value.zh: 武帝受禪，封濟南王。
value.en: Sima Yan created Jinan prince.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Jinan.

value.zh: 泰始二年薨。
value.en: He died in the second year of Taishi.
value.literal: In the second year of Taishi, he died.

value.zh: 二子：耽、緝。
value.en: Sons Dan and Ji.
value.literal: Two sons: Dan and Ji.

value.zh: 耽嗣立，咸寧三年徙為中山王。
value.en: Dan succeeded to the title, and in Xianning year three he was transferred to be Prince of Zhongshan.
value.literal: Dan succeeded to the title, and in Xianning year three he was transferred to be Prince of Zhongshan.

value.zh: 是年薨，無子，緝繼。
value.en: Dan died childless same year; Ji followed.
value.literal: Same year died without sons Ji continued.

value.zh: 成都王穎以緝為建威將軍，與石熙等率眾距王浚，沒於陣，薨。
value.en: Ying named Ji bulwark general alongside Shi Xi to stop Wang Jun; Ji died on the field.
value.literal: Prince of Chengdu Ying appointed Ji bulwark general leading hosts with Shi Xi resisting Wang Jun perishing in battle.

value.zh: 無子，國除。
value.en: Without heirs the principality ended.
value.literal: Having no sons state abolished.

value.zh: 譙剛王遜，字子悌，宣帝弟魏中郎進之子也。
value.en: Sima Xun, styled Ziti, was the son of Sima Jin, Sima Yi's younger brother.
value.literal: Prince Gang of Qiao Xun courtesy Ziti was son of Sima Jin—Emperor Xuan's younger brother who served Wei as gentleman of the palace.

value.zh: 仕魏關內侯，改封城陽亭侯，參鎮東軍事，拜輕車將軍、羽林左監。
value.en: Under Wei he rose through marquis ranks to light-chariot general and guard superintendent on the eastern army staff.
value.literal: Serving Wei he held district marquis within the passes, was reassigned marquis of Chengyang precinct, joined the eastern garrison staff, and was appointed general of light chariots and left superintendent of the imperial guard.

value.zh: 五等建，徙封涇陽男。
value.en: Five ranks moved him to Jingyang baron.
value.literal: When five ranks established transferred enfeoffment Jingyang baron.

value.zh: 武帝受禪，封譙王，邑四千四百戶。
value.en: Sima Yan made him prince of Qiao at 4,400 households.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication enfeoffed Prince of Qiao four thousand four hundred households.

value.zh: 泰始二年薨。
value.en: He died in the second year of Taishi.
value.literal: In the second year of Taishi, he died.

value.zh: 二子：隨、承。
value.en: Sons Sui and Cheng.
value.literal: Two sons: Sui and Cheng.

value.zh: 定王隨立。
value.en: Prince Ding Sima Sui inherited.
value.literal: Prince Ding Sui succeeded.

value.zh: 薨，子邃立，沒于石勒，元帝以承嗣遜。
value.en: When the heir was lost to Shi Le, Sima Rui transferred the succession to Sima Cheng.
value.literal: He died; his heir succeeded but fell captive to Shi Le, so Yuan Di appointed Cheng to continue Xun's line.

value.zh: 任城景王陵，字子山，宣帝弟魏司隸從事安城亭侯通之子也。
value.en: Sima Ling, styled Zishan, was son of Sima Tong—Sima Yi's nephew.
value.literal: Prince Jing of Rencheng Ling courtesy Zishan was son of Emperor Xuan's younger brother Wei clerk of provincial investigator Marquis of Ancheng precinct Tong.

value.zh: 初拜議郎。
value.en: He began as gentleman consultant.
value.literal: At first appointed gentleman consultant.

value.zh: 泰始元年封北海王，邑四千七百戶。
value.en: In the first year of Taishi, he received Beihai at 4,700 households.
value.literal: In the first year of Taishi, Enfeoffed Prince of Beihai four thousand seven hundred households.

value.zh: 三年，轉封任城王，之國。
value.en: Year three moved him to Rencheng with orders to his domain.
value.literal: Third year transferred enfeoffment Prince of Rencheng proceeding state.

value.zh: 咸寧五年薨，子濟立。
value.en: In the fifth year of Xianning, his son Ji inherited.
value.literal: In the fifth year of Xianning, Died son Ji succeeded.

value.zh: 拜散騎侍郎、給事中、散騎常侍、輔國將軍。
value.en: Ji rose through palace attendant posts to bulwark general.
value.literal: Appointed irregular cavalry gentleman consultant irregular cavalry attendant bulwark general.

value.zh: 隨東海王越在項，為石勒所害，二子俱沒。
value.en: At Xiang with Sima Yue he fell to Shi Le with both sons.
value.literal: Following Prince of Donghai Yue at Xiang harmed by Shi Le two sons together lost.

value.zh: 有二弟：順、斌。
value.en: Two brothers: Shun and Bin.
value.literal: Had two younger brothers Shun Bin.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
value.en: Sima Yu, styled Xizu, was Emperor Hui's firstborn—his mother was Lady Xie of Talented rank.
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

value.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
value.en: Wu Di doted on the bright boy and kept him always near.
value.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

value.zh: 嘗與諸皇子共戲殿上，惠帝來朝，執諸皇子手，次至太子，帝曰：「是汝兒也。」
value.en: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience, he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, the emperor said, 'This is your son.'
value.literal: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'

value.zh: 惠帝乃止。
value.en: Hui broke off his greeting.
value.literal: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.

value.zh: 宮中嘗夜失火，武帝登樓望之。
value.en: A night blaze drew Wu Di to a high gallery.
value.literal: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.

value.zh: 太子時年五歲，牽帝裾入暗中。
value.en: Five-year-old Yu pulled his grandfather into the dark.
value.literal: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.

value.zh: 帝問其故，太子曰：「暮夜倉卒，宜備非常，不宜令照見人君也。」
value.en: The crown prince said, "Suddenly at night one must guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face."
value.literal: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'

value.zh: 由是奇之。
value.en: Wu Di marked him extraordinary.
value.literal: From this Wu Di marveled at him.

value.zh: 嘗從帝觀豕牢，言於帝曰：「豕甚肥，何不殺以享士，而使久費五穀？」
value.en: While watching the imperial sty he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"
value.literal: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, 'The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?'

value.zh: 帝嘉其意，即使烹之。
value.en: Wu Di approved and had them slaughtered.
value.literal: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.

value.zh: 因撫其背，謂廷尉傅祗曰：「此兒當興我家。」
value.en: He stroked the boy's back and told Court Commandant Fu Zhi, "This child will bring prosperity to our house."
value.literal: He therefore stroked the boy's back and said to Court Commandant Fu Zhi, 'This child will bring prosperity to our house.'

value.zh: 嘗對群臣稱太子似宣帝，於是令譽流於天下。
value.en: He likened the heir to Sima Yi before court—reputation followed.
value.literal: He once declared before the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan; thereafter praise of him spread through the realm.

value.zh: 序
value.en: Preface
value.literal: Preface

value.zh: 魯芝，字世英，扶風郿人也。
value.en: Lu Zhi (courtesy Shiying) came from Mei county in Fufeng.
value.literal: Lu Zhi, courtesy name Shiying, was a native of Mei in Fufeng.

value.zh: 世有名德，為西州豪族。
value.en: His clan had long been celebrated for integrity and ranked among the great houses of the northwest.
value.literal: For generations his family had enjoyed renowned virtue and was a powerful clan of the western provinces.

value.zh: 父為郭氾所害，芝繈褓流離，年十七，乃移居雍，耽思墳籍。
value.en: Guo Si murdered his father; Zhi was still an infant when the family was scattered. At seventeen he settled in Yong and buried himself in the canon.
value.literal: His father was killed by Guo Si; Zhi, still in swaddling clothes, wandered destitute, and at seventeen he moved to Yong, immersing himself in study of the classics.

value.zh: 郡舉上計吏，州辟別駕。
value.en: The commandery nominated him accounts clerk; the province called him up as provincial aide.
value.literal: The commandery recommended him as clerk for the annual accounting; the province summoned him as provincial aide.

value.zh: 魏車騎將軍郭淮為雍州刺史，深敬重之。
value.en: Wei general Guo Huai, as inspector of Yong, treated him with exceptional respect.
value.literal: Guo Huai, General of Chariots and Cavalry of Wei, was Inspector of Yong Province and held him in deep respect.

value.zh: 舉孝廉，除郎中。
value.en: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he received a gentleman-of-the-interior appointment.
value.literal: He was recommended as filial and incorrupt and appointed gentleman of the interior.

value.zh: 會蜀相諸葛亮侵隴右，淮復請芝為別駕。
value.en: When Zhuge Liang of Shu struck Longyou, Guo Huai again kept him on as provincial aide.
value.literal: When the Shu chancellor Zhuge Liang invaded Longyou, Huai again asked Zhi to serve as provincial aide.

value.zh: 事平，薦於公府，辟大司馬曹真掾，轉臨淄侯文學。
value.en: After hostilities ended he went to the central ministries, served as staff to Grand Marshal Cao Zhen, then moved to tutor of literature for the marquis of Linzi.
value.literal: When the affair was settled, [Zhi] was recommended to the ministerial offices and summoned as aide to the Grand Marshal Cao Zhen; he was transferred to literary instructor to the Marquis of Linzi.

value.zh: 鄭袤薦于司空王朗，朗即加禮命。
value.en: Zheng Mao introduced him to Wang Lang, minister of works, who honored him with an immediate posting.
value.literal: Zheng Mao recommended him to Minister of Works Wang Lang, and Lang at once treated him with courtesy and appointed him.

value.zh: 後拜騎都尉、參軍事、行安南太守，遷尚書郎。
value.en: He rose through Commandant of Cavalry, military adviser, acting administrator of An'nan, and gentleman at the Masters of Writing.
value.literal: Later he was appointed Commandant of Cavalry, joined military affairs, acted as Administrator of An'nan, was promoted to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

value.zh: 曹真出督關右，又參大司馬軍事。
value.en: When Cao Zhen supervised the region west of the passes, Zhi again served on the grand marshal's staff.
value.literal: When Cao Zhen went out to supervise the west of the Pass, [Zhi] again joined the Grand Marshal's military staff.

value.zh: 真薨，宣帝代焉，乃引芝參驃騎軍事，轉天水太守。
value.en: After Cao Zhen died Sima Yi took his place and attached Zhi to the agile-cavalry command; Zhi then became administrator of Tianshui.
value.literal: When Zhen died, the Emperor Xuan [Sima Yi] replaced him and then brought Zhi in to join the military staff of the General of Agile Cavalry; [Zhi] was transferred to Administrator of Tianshui.

value.zh: 郡鄰於蜀，數被侵掠，戶口減削，寇盜充斥，芝傾心鎮衛，更造城市，數年間舊境悉復。
value.en: Tianshui lay against Shu and suffered repeated raids: population fell and bandits multiplied. Zhi threw himself into defense, rebuilt the city, and within a few years the district recovered its old bounds.
value.literal: The commandery bordered Shu and repeatedly suffered invasion and plunder; households dwindled and bandits swarmed. Zhi devoted himself to guarding and defending, rebuilt the walls and town, and within a few years the former territory was fully restored.

value.zh: 遷廣平太守。
value.en: He was transferred to Guangping.
value.literal: He was promoted to Administrator of Guangping.

value.zh: 天水夷夏慕德，老幼赴闕獻書，乞留芝。
value.en: Yi tribesmen and Han alike cherished him; young and old traveled to the capital with petitions begging the court to keep him.
value.literal: Both Yi and Han Chinese in Tianshui admired his virtue; old and young went to the capital to submit petitions asking that Zhi be kept [in office].

value.zh: 魏明帝許焉，仍策書嘉歎，勉以黃霸之美，加討寇將軍。
value.en: Emperor Ming agreed, issued a warm commendation comparing him to Huang Ba, and added the title General Who Suppresses Brigands.
value.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei granted this; an edict was still issued praising him, encouraging him with the fine example of Huang Ba, and he was additionally granted the title General Who Suppresses Brigands.

value.zh: 曹爽輔政，引為司馬。
value.en: When Cao Shuang controlled the regency he took Zhi on as marshal.
value.literal: When Cao Shuang dominated the government, [Shuang] brought [Zhi] in as marshal.

value.zh: 芝屢有讜言嘉謀，爽弗能納。
value.en: Zhi gave blunt, sound advice again and again; Shuang refused to listen.
value.literal: Zhi repeatedly offered forthright counsel and fine plans, which Shuang could not accept.

value.zh: 及宣帝起兵誅爽，芝率餘眾犯門斬關，馳出赴爽，勸爽曰：「公居伊周之位，一旦以罪見黜，雖欲牽黃犬，復可得乎！
value.en: When the Emperor Xuan [Sima Yi] raised troops to execute Shuang, Zhi led the remaining troops to force the gates and break through the barriers, galloping out to join Shuang, and urged Shuang: 'You occupy the position of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—once you are dismissed for crime, even if you wished to lead a yellow dog [on a hunt], could you have it again?
value.literal: When the Emperor Xuan [Sima Yi] raised troops to execute Shuang, Zhi led the remaining troops to force the gates and break through the barriers, galloping out to join Shuang, and urged Shuang: 'You occupy the position of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—once you are dismissed for crime, even if you wished to lead a yellow dog [on a hunt], could you have it again?

value.zh: 若挾天子保許昌，杖大威以羽檄征四方兵，孰敢不從！
value.en: If you seize the Son of Heaven and hold Xuchang, wielding great awe and dispatching feathered summons to levy troops from the four quarters, who would dare not follow?
value.literal: If you seize the Son of Heaven and hold Xuchang, wielding great awe and dispatching feathered summons to levy troops from the four quarters, who would dare not follow?

value.zh: 舍此而去，欲就東市，豈不痛哉！」
value.en: To abandon this and depart, only to go to the eastern market [for execution]—how could it not be bitter?'
value.literal: To abandon this and depart, only to go to the eastern market [for execution]—how could it not be bitter?'

value.zh: 爽懦惑不能用，遂委身受戮。
value.en: Shuang was timid and bewildered and ignored him; he surrendered and died under the blade.
value.literal: Shuang was cowardly and confused and could not use [the advice]; he thereupon submitted his person and was executed.

value.zh: 芝坐爽下獄，當死，而口不訟直，志不苟免。
value.en: Zhi, tied to Shuang's faction, went to prison facing death, yet he neither whined for mercy nor grasped at an unworthy reprieve.
value.literal: Zhi, implicated under Shuang, was imprisoned and sentenced to death, yet he did not argue his innocence aloud and was resolved not to seek escape unworthily.

value.zh: 宣帝嘉之，赦而不誅。
value.en: Sima Yi admired him and spared his life.
value.literal: The Emperor Xuan admired him and pardoned him without execution.

value.zh: 俄而起為使持節、領護匈奴中郎將、振威將軍、并州刺史。
value.en: Soon he held credentials as commissioner, concurrent colonel of the central Xiongnu corps, General Who Rouses Might, and inspector of Bing.
value.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed commissioner with credentials, concurrent Colonel for the Xiongnu of the Center, General Who Rouses Might, and Inspector of Bing Province.

value.zh: 以綏緝有方，遷大鴻臚。
value.en: His skill at pacifying and administering won him promotion to grand herald.
value.literal: For skilled pacification and administration he was promoted to Grand Herald.

value.zh: 若夫穹昊垂景，少微以躔其次；
value.en: Consider how the high heavens let fall their light, and the hermit star Shaowei keeps to its station in the sky.
value.literal: As for the vaulted heaven lowering its radiance, Shaowei thereby treads its place among them;

value.zh: 《文》《系》探幽，貞遁以成其象。
value.en: The "Appended Remarks" and "Wings" sound out what lies in shadow, and the hexagram of principled retreat gives that stance its perfect emblem.
value.literal: The "Wen" and "Xi" plumb the hidden; steadfast withdrawal completes their image.

value.zh: 故有避於言色，其道聞乎孔公；
value.en: Hence men who gave nothing away in word or look, whose path we know because Confucius spoke of them;
value.literal: Therefore there were those who avoided it in speech and countenance; of their way one hears from the Duke Kong;

value.zh: 驕乎富貴，厥義詳于孫子。
value.en: and the proud scorning of wealth and station, whose moral sense Sunzi laid out at length.
value.literal: As for pride toward wealth and noble rank, its meaning was set forth in detail by Master Sun.

value.zh: 是以處柔伊存，有生之恆性；
value.en: To hold to yielding strength is how life endures; that is the fixed temper of everything that breathes;
value.literal: Therefore to abide in softness is how it endures; it is the constant nature of the living;

value.zh: 在盈斯害，惟神之常道。
value.en: while fullness invites injury—such has always been heaven's steady law.
value.literal: to be at fullness is thereby harm; it is the constant way of the spirit.

value.zh: 古先智士體其若茲，介焉超俗，浩然養素，藏聲江海之上，卷跡囂氛之表，漱流而激其清，寢巢而韜其耀，良畫以符其志，絕機以虛其心。
value.en: Men of old who grasped this truth stood aloof from the crowd, breathed in a clarity that nourished plain living, let their names die away beyond the rivers and seas, and withdrew their footsteps from the world's noise. They drank from running water to keep themselves clean, dwelt like birds in the wild to dim their luster, chose their course with deliberate care, and stilled every scheme so the heart could rest empty.
value.literal: Ancient wise men embodied it thus: standing apart they transcended the vulgar, in vast purity they nurtured simplicity, they hid their voices above the rivers and seas, they rolled up their traces beyond the clamor and dust, they rinsed their mouths in the current to quicken its clearness, they slept in nests to sheathe their brilliance, they took fine plans to match their intent, they cut off contrivance to empty their hearts.

value.zh: 玉輝冰潔，川渟岳峙，修至樂之道，固無疆之休，長往邈而不追，安排窅而無悶，修身自保，悔吝弗生，詩人《考槃》之歌，抑在茲矣。
value.en: They shone like jade and held the chill of ice; they were still as a held river, steadfast as a mountain. They walked the path of deepest contentment and won a peace without end. Once they had gone far, none could overtake them; they accepted whatever came, untroubled in the dark. Guarding the person, they kept harm away—no cause for remorse—and the ode the Classic of Poetry calls "Kao pan" might almost have been written of them.
value.literal: Jade radiance, ice purity; like a river at rest, like a peak standing; they cultivated the way of supreme joy, they secured boundless good fortune; long gone, remote, none could pursue them; settled in the depths, without vexation; they cultivated the self to preserve themselves, regret and shame did not arise—the poet's song of "Kao pan," is it not here?

value.zh: 至於體天作制之後，訟息刑清之時，尚乃仄席幽貞以康神化，徵聘之禮賁於岩穴，玉帛之贄委於窒衡，故《月令》曰：「季春之月聘名士，禮賢者」，斯之謂歟！
value.en: Even once a ruler had aligned his government with heaven and the courts fell quiet, he would still leave the high seat half-empty for recluses of firm integrity, so culture might flourish. Envoys climbed to mountain huts; jade and silk waited on the doorsteps of the poor. That is why the "Monthly Ordinances" says that in late spring one should call forth noted scholars and honor the wise—surely it speaks of just such a time.
value.literal: As for after one embodied heaven and established institutions, at the time when lawsuits ceased and punishments were clear, still one vacated the mat for the hidden and steadfast to perfect spiritual transformation; the rites of summons and appointment shone into cliffside caves, gifts of jade and silk piled at humble doors—therefore the "Monthly Ordinances" says, "In the last month of spring one hires eminent scholars and treats the worthy with ritual"—does it not mean this?

value.zh: 自典午運開，旁求隱逸，譙元彥之杜絕人事，江思悛之嘯詠林藪，峻其貞白之軌，成其出塵之跡，雖不應其嘉招，亦足激其貪競。
value.en: Since the house of Jin rose, the throne has combed the hills for hidden men: Qiao Xiu shut his gate on the world, Jiang Dun whistled and sang deep in the hills. They raised the standard of unstained integrity and showed how to step outside the scramble for power. They never took the court's gracious offers, yet their example was enough to shame the grasping and the ambitious.
value.literal: From when the Jin fortune opened, seeking far and wide for recluses, as with Qiao Xiuyuan's cutting off human affairs, or Jiang Silun's whistling and chanting in woods and marshes, they made steep the track of chastity and purity, they completed traces beyond the dust; although they did not respond to fine summons, still it was enough to sting greed and rivalry.

value.zh: 今美其高尚之德，綴集於篇。
value.en: Here I gather their stories to honor the height of their character.
value.literal: Now I praise their lofty virtue and string them together in this chapter.

value.zh: 范粲，字承明，陳留外黃人，漢萊蕪長丹之孫也。
value.en: Fan Can, courtesy name Chengming, was from Waihuang in Chenliu—a grandson of Fan Dan, who had been magistrate of Laiwu under the Han.
value.literal: Fan Can, styled Chengming, was a man of Waihuang in Chenliu, a grandson of Fan Dan, magistrate of Laiwu in Han.

value.zh: 粲高亮貞正，有丹風，而博涉強記，學皆可師，遠近請益者甚眾，性不矜莊，而見之皆肅如也。
value.en: He was as stern and honest as his grandfather Fan Dan, with a memory that drank in books. Students flocked to him from every quarter. He wore no air of pomp, yet everyone who met him stood straighter.
value.literal: Can was lofty, bright, chaste, and upright; he had Dan's bearing, yet was broadly read with a strong memory, and all his learning could serve as a model; those near and far who sought instruction were very many; by nature he was not stiffly solemn, yet all who saw him were awed.

value.zh: 魏時州府交辟，皆無所就。
value.en: During the Wei, provincial and commandery posts came again and again; he refused them all.
value.literal: In Wei times the province and prefecture repeatedly summoned him; he took none of the posts.

value.zh: 久之，乃應命為治中，轉別駕，辟太尉掾、尚書郎，出為征西司馬，所曆職皆有聲稱。
value.en: At length he accepted a place as administrative adviser, rose to chief clerk, served as aide to the grand commandant and gentleman of the palace, then marched west as army marshal—winning praise in each office.
value.literal: After a long while he then answered appointment as administrative adviser, transferred to chief clerk, was summoned as aide to the grand commandant and as gentleman of the palace, then went out as marshal on the western campaign; in every post he held he had a fine reputation.

value.zh: 及宣帝輔政，遷武威太守。
value.en: When Emperor Xuan took charge of the regency, Can was named governor of Wuwei.
value.literal: When Emperor Xuan assisted the government, he was moved to governor of Wuwei.

value.zh: 到郡，選良吏，立學校，勸農桑。
value.en: There he picked able officers, opened schools, and pushed farming and silk work.
value.literal: Arriving in the commandery, he selected good clerks, established schools, and urged farming and sericulture.

value.zh: 是時戎夷頗侵疆場，粲明設防備，敵不敢犯，西域流通，無烽燧之警。
value.en: Barbarians harried the frontier, but his clear dispositions kept them out; the Silk Road stayed open and the signal fires stayed cold.
value.literal: At that time the Rong and Yi often raided the borders; Can clearly set defenses so the enemy did not dare attack; the Western Regions flowed through trade and there was no alarm from beacon fires.

value.zh: 又郡壤富實，珍玩充積，粲檢制之，息其華侈。
value.en: The prefecture was rich and temptation everywhere; he tightened discipline and cut back extravagance.
value.literal: Moreover the commandery soil was rich and treasures filled the storehouses; Can checked and regulated this and stilled its luxury.

value.zh: 以母老罷官。
value.en: He left office when his mother grew frail.
value.literal: Because his mother was old he resigned office.

value.zh: 郡既接近寇戎，粲又重鎮輒去職，朝廷尤之，左遷樂涫令。
value.en: The court faulted him for walking away from a sensitive post on the barbarian edge and demoted him to magistrate of Leku.
value.literal: The commandery being close to raiding enemies, and Can again a key stronghold who abruptly left his post, the court blamed him and demoted him to magistrate of Leku.

value.zh: 頃之，轉太宰從事中郎。
value.en: Soon he was shifted to retainer clerk under the grand steward.
value.literal: Before long he was transferred to retainer clerk with the grand steward.

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to retainer clerk with the grand steward.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was shifted to retainer clerk under the grand steward.

value.zh: 遭母憂，以至孝稱。
value.en: His mother's death plunged him into mourning famed for its grief.
value.literal: He encountered mourning for his mother and was famed for utmost filial piety.

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for his mother and was famed for utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's death plunged him into mourning famed for its grief.

value.zh: 服闕，復為太宰中郎。
value.en: When the mourning term ended he returned as the steward's clerk.
value.literal: When mourning was ended, he again became steward's retainer.

translations.literal: When mourning was ended, he again became steward's retainer.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning term ended he returned as the steward's clerk.

value.zh: 齊王芳被廢，遷于金墉城，粲素服拜送，哀慟左右。
value.en: When Cao Fang, the prince of Qi, was cast down and sent to the Metal Rampart palace, Can went in undyed linen to bow him off and wept until bystanders wept with him.
value.literal: When Prince Qi of Cao Fang was deposed and moved to the Metal-walled City, Can in plain garb bowed in farewell, grieving so that those around him were moved.

source.zh: 齊王芳被廢，遷于金墉城，粲素服拜送，哀慟左右。

translations.literal: When Prince Qi of Cao Fang was deposed and moved to the Metal-walled City, Can in plain garb bowed in farewell, grieving so that those around him were moved.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Fang, the prince of Qi, was cast down and sent to the Metal Rampart palace, Can went in undyed linen to bow him off and wept until bystanders wept with him.

value.zh: 時景帝輔政，召群官會議，粲又不到，朝廷以其時望，優容之。
value.en: Emperor Jing called a plenary council; Can stayed away again, yet the court indulged him because of his moral weight.
value.literal: At the time Emperor Jing assisted the government, he summoned the officials to a joint conference; Can again did not arrive; the court, because of his contemporary prestige, treated him leniently.

source.zh: 時景帝輔政，召群官會議，粲又不到，朝廷以其時望，優容之。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Jing assisted the government, he summoned the officials to a joint conference; Can again did not arrive; the court, because of his contemporary prestige, treated him leniently.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing called a plenary council; Can stayed away again, yet the court indulged him because of his moral weight.

value.zh: 粲又稱疾，闔門不出。
value.en: He pleaded illness once more and barred his gate.
value.literal: Can again pleaded illness and shut his gate, not going out.

translations.literal: Can again pleaded illness and shut his gate, not going out.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness once more and barred his gate.

value.zh: 於是特詔為侍中，持節使於雍州。
value.en: A special edict named him palace attendant with credentials and ordered him to Yongzhou.
value.literal: Thereupon a special edict made him palace attendant with staff of authority and sent him on mission to Yongzhou.

source.zh: 於是特詔為侍中，持節使於雍州。

translations.literal: Thereupon a special edict made him palace attendant with staff of authority and sent him on mission to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict named him palace attendant with credentials and ordered him to Yongzhou.

value.zh: 粲因陽狂不言，寢所乘車，足不履地。
value.en: He feigned madness and fell silent, living in his carriage so his feet never touched earth.
value.literal: Can therefore feigned madness and would not speak; he slept in the carriage he rode and his feet did not touch the ground.

source.zh: 粲因陽狂不言，寢所乘車，足不履地。

translations.literal: Can therefore feigned madness and would not speak; he slept in the carriage he rode and his feet did not touch the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned madness and fell silent, living in his carriage so his feet never touched earth.

value.zh: 子孫恆侍左右，至有婚宦大事，輒密諮焉。
value.en: Sons and grandsons waited on him always; even weddings and appointments they settled only after whispered questions at his pillow.
value.literal: His sons and grandsons constantly attended at his side; even for great matters of marriage or office they secretly consulted him.

source.zh: 子孫恆侍左右，至有婚宦大事，輒密諮焉。

translations.literal: His sons and grandsons constantly attended at his side; even for great matters of marriage or office they secretly consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Sons and grandsons waited on him always; even weddings and appointments they settled only after whispered questions at his pillow.

value.zh: 合者則色無變，不合則眠寢不安，妻子以此知其旨。
value.en: If he approved, his face stayed calm; if not, he tossed all night—so his household read his mind.
value.literal: If it agreed, his color did not change; if it did not agree, then his sleep was restless; by this his wife and children knew his intent.

source.zh: 合者則色無變，不合則眠寢不安，妻子以此知其旨。

translations.literal: If it agreed, his color did not change; if it did not agree, then his sleep was restless; by this his wife and children knew his intent.
translations.idiomatic: If he approved, his face stayed calm; if not, he tossed all night—so his household read his mind.

value.zh: 唐禮：四時各以孟月享太廟，每室用太牢，季冬蠟祭之後，以辰日臘享於太廟，用牲如時祭。
value.en: Tang ritual: each season's first month, offerings at the Great Temple—tai lao per chamber. After twelfth-month wax and la, a chen-day la feast at the temple used seasonal victims.
value.literal: Tang rites: In each of the four seasons, in the first month of the season, offerings were made to the Great Ancestral Temple; for each chamber the great offering was used. After the wax sacrifices following the twelfth month's la rites, on a chen day a la offering was presented at the Great Temple, with victims as at the seasonal sacrifices.

value.zh: 三年一祫，以孟冬。
value.en: A he rite every three years, in mid-winter's opening month.
value.literal: Every three years a he sacrifice, in the first month of winter.

value.zh: 五年一禘，以孟夏。
value.en: A di rite every five years, in mid-summer's opening month.
value.literal: Every five years a di sacrifice, in the first month of summer.

value.zh: 又時享之日，修七祀於太廟西門內之道南：司命，戶以春，灶以夏；
value.en: On seasonal offering days the Seven Sacrifices were kept on the lane south of the temple's west gate—Spirit of Fate; Household Spirit in spring, Stove Spirit in summer;
value.literal: On days of seasonal offerings, the Seven Sacrifices were maintained on the road south within the western gate of the Great Temple: Spirit of Fate; the Household Spirit in spring, the Stove Spirit in summer;

value.zh: 門，厲以秋，行以冬，中溜則于季夏迎氣日祀之。
value.en: Gate and Pestilence Spirits in autumn, Road Spirit in winter; Central Gutter on the last-summer qi-reception day.
value.literal: the Gate Spirit and the Pestilence Spirit in autumn, the Road Spirit in winter; the Central Gutter was sacrificed on the day of receiving seasonal qi in the last month of summer.

value.zh: 若品物時新堪進御者，所司先送太常，與尚食相知，簡擇精好者，以滋味與新物相宜者配之。
value.en: Seasonal delicacies fit for the throne went first to the Court of Sacrifices and the Provisioners, who picked the best and matched flavor to the new offering.
value.literal: If seasonal novelties were fit to present to the sovereign, the responsible office first sent them to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and coordinated with the Imperial Provisioners, selecting the finest and pairing them with flavors suited to the new goods.

value.zh: 太常卿奉薦於太廟，不出神主。
value.en: The Minister of Sacrifices presented at the Great Temple without removing the tablets.
value.literal: The Minister of Imperial Sacrifices presented offerings at the Great Temple without bringing out the spirit tablets.

value.zh: 仲春薦冰，亦如之。
value.en: Mid-spring ice offerings followed the same rule.
value.literal: In mid-spring ice was presented—in the same manner.

value.zh: 中宗即位，神龍元年正月，改享德廟依舊為京太廟。
value.en: After Zhongzong's accession, Shenlong 1, first month restored Xiangde Temple as the capital Grand Temple.
value.literal: After Zhongzong took the throne, in the first month of the first year of Shenlong, Xiangde Temple was changed back into the capital Grand Temple as before.

value.zh: 五月，遷武氏七廟神主於西京之崇尊廟，東都創置太廟。
value.en: Fifth month: seven Wu tablets went to western Chongzun; a new Great Temple rose at the eastern capital.
value.literal: Fifth month: moved the seven Wu clan temple spirit tablets to western capital Chongzun Temple; newly established Great Temple at eastern capital.

value.zh: 太常博士張齊賢建議曰：昔孫卿子云：「有天下者事七代，有一國者事五代。」
value.en: Grand Ritual Erudite Zhang Qixian cited Xunzi: "The ruler of All Under Heaven serves seven generations; the ruler of one state serves five."
value.literal: Grand Ritual Erudite Zhang Qixian cited Xunzi: "The ruler of All Under Heaven serves seven generations; the ruler of one state serves five."

value.zh: 則天子七廟，古今達禮。
value.en: Thus the emperor has seven temples, a ritual standard accepted across antiquity and the present.
value.literal: Thus the emperor has seven temples, a ritual standard accepted across antiquity and the present.

value.zh: 故《尚書》稱「七代之廟，可以觀德」。
value.en: 《Documents》 says, "Through seven generations of temples, one may observe virtue."
value.literal: 《Documents》 says, "Through seven generations of temples, one may observe virtue."

value.zh: 《祭法》稱「王立七廟，一壇一墠」。
value.en: 《Sacrificial Regulations》 says, "The king establishes seven temples, one altar, and one open ground."
value.literal: 《Sacrificial Regulations》 says, "The king establishes seven temples, one altar, and one open ground."

value.zh: 《王制》云：「天子七廟，三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七。」
value.en: The 《Wang System》 says, "The Son of Heaven has seven temples: three zhao, three mu, and the Grand Ancestor's temple."
value.literal: The 《Wang System》 says, "The Son of Heaven has seven temples: three zhao, three mu, and the Grand Ancestor's temple."

value.zh: 莫不尊始封之君，謂之太祖。
value.en: All such systems honor the first enfeoffed lord as Grand Ancestor.
value.literal: All such systems honor the first enfeoffed lord as Grand Ancestor.

value.zh: 太祖之廟，百代不遷。
value.en: The Grand Ancestor's temple remains unmoved for a hundred generations.
value.literal: The Grand Ancestor's temple remains unmoved for a hundred generations.
